domains.name: Accounts and access
domains.description: Who people are, the accounts they share, and what each may do.
domains.body:
Everyone has one account, whichever hats they wear: a client's member, one of
Exalynt's engineers, a partner, or several at once. Clients' organizations are
kept apart from each other, and what someone may do in each comes from their
role there.

domains.name: Agreements
domains.description: The terms each client, engineer and partnership works with Exalynt under.
domains.body:
Each party reads and accepts its own agreement before it can work: a Client
Agreement for an organization, an Engineer Agreement for an engineer, and a
Partner Agreement for a partnership.

domains.name: Billing
domains.description: Charging clients for the capacity they buy.
domains.body:
The payment provider holds payment methods, billing details and invoices, and
works out the tax on each invoice. Exalynt never calculates tax itself.

domains.name: Engineering capacity
domains.description: Selling engineering capacity in blocks, and scheduling, staffing and delivering it week by week.
domains.body:
Clients see capacity in units and blocks, never hours: a unit is a quarter of
one engineer's week. What a week has room for comes from what the engineers on
a client's teams offer.

domains.name: Partnerships
domains.description: The Partnership Program: partners who bring Exalynt clients, and earn on them.
domains.body:
A partnership is a partner's own record, separate from any client
organization. The clients it brings are attributed to it, and it earns on
their blocks for a while after.

domains.name: Earnings and pay
domains.description: What people and partnerships earn from each block, and getting it to them.
domains.body:
An earning is what someone is owed for a block. A payout is money sent, made up
of earnings, once an admin has released it.

features.name: Client organizations

features.name: Onboarding
features.description: Bringing clients, engineers and partners in, and getting each ready to work.
features.body:
## Clients

A business signs up on its own and gets to its first block booked into a week:

1. Someone at the business signs up, without an invitation, and creates an
   organization.
2. One of its Admins accepts the
   [Client Agreement](../../agreements/capabilities/client-agreements.md) on its
   behalf, before anyone can use the portal for it.
3. Exalynt gives the organization a team as it signs up, when one has an
   engineer offering time. If none does, it waits without a team until an admin
   assigns one, and can still buy.
4. The client sees what's still needed before work can start, and adds a
   payment method and company details.
5. They [buy a block](../../capacity/capabilities/capacity-purchasing.md), and
   [schedule it](../../capacity/capabilities/scheduling.md) for a preferred
   week.

A client who signed up with a partner's referral code, link or invitation is
attributed to that partnership, and told when signing up that the partner may
earn from it. Others join later by an Admin's invitation, each with a role.

## Engineers

An admin invites the engineer by email, choosing their team, if any, and
setting the Commercial Terms of their
[Engineer Agreement](../../agreements/capabilities/engineer-agreements.md). The
engineer accepts, signing up first if they need to, reads and accepts the
agreement, and then sets their availability, the bank account their payouts go
to, and a short bio, until they're ready for client work. Someone who already
has an account keeps it, and gains the console alongside what they had.

## Partners

How partners are enrolled is part of the
[Partner program](../../partnerships/features/partner-program.md).

features.name: Block delivery
features.description: Getting each block a client buys scheduled into a week, staffed by an engineer, and worked until it's fulfilled.
features.body:
## How it goes

1. The client schedules the block for a preferred week that has room.
2. An engineer claims it from the client's shared queue, or an admin assigns
   an eligible engineer to it.
3. The engineer starts it, any time from the start of its week, and can add a
   focus saying what its work is about, unless the client already has.
4. The engineer marks it fulfilled. Nobody reviews it, and the client sees it
   go from in progress to fulfilled.
5. The people who earned from it see what it earned them, and are paid once an
   admin releases the week's payouts. That's
   [Getting paid](../../pay/features/getting-paid.md).

A block the client moves before its week starts comes off its engineer and goes
back to the shared queue for its new week. A block nobody is on when its week
ends stays scheduled and still owed, and an admin moves it to a coming week.

features.name: Buying capacity
features.description: Helping clients see what a project might take, buy the capacity for it, and follow where it stands.

features.name: Clients and teams
features.description: Organizing Exalynt's engineers into teams, knowing what each offers, and matching teams with the clients they serve.

features.name: Partner program
features.description: Bringing Exalynt clients through partners, and paying partners for the clients they bring.
features.body:
## Enrolling a partner

1. An admin invites the partner by email and sets the partnership's terms. The
   invitation creates a new partnership for them to manage.
2. The partner signs up, if they need to, and reads the
   [Partner Agreement](../../agreements/capabilities/partner-agreements.md) the
   invitation offers.
3. They name the partnership and accept, in one step: that accepts the
   invitation and the Partner Agreement together.
4. They see the partnership's terms, and its referral code and sign-up link to
   share, or invite people by email.
5. They see what's left before they can be paid, and set up the
   [payout account](../../pay/capabilities/partner-payout-accounts.md) the
   partnership's earnings go to.

Someone who already has an account keeps it. A partner who manages several
partnerships switches between them, viewing one at a time.

features.name: Getting paid
features.description: Paying the people who earned from each block: the engineer on it, their team lead and their teammates, each by their own Engineer Agreement.
features.body:
Each week's payouts are seen by an admin before they're sent, and go out once
the admin releases them. An earning that can't be paid is held, with what needs
fixing, and a failed payout is sent again.

features.name: Partner program
features.description: Bringing Exalynt clients through partners, and paying partners for the clients they bring.
features.body:
Pay's part of the program: what a partnership earns on its clients' blocks, and
paying it to the partnership's own account, never its manager's.

capabilities.name: Access tokens
capabilities.description: People create personal access tokens so their scripts and tools can call the API as them, everywhere they belong or only in the organizations they choose.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Everyone lists and revokes their personal access tokens.
- Everyone sees where each of their tokens works.

capabilities.name: Engineer onboarding
capabilities.description: Engineers join Exalynt by an admin's invitation, on the team it names if it names one, since nobody signs up as an engineer on their own.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers sign up to accept their invitation, if they don't have an account
  yet.
- Engineers see the terms that set their engineer share.

capabilities.name: Getting set up
capabilities.description: People see what they still have to set up: a client before work can start, an engineer before they're ready for client work, and a partner before they can be paid.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see what's still needed, such as an assigned engineering team, a
  payment method, company details, capacity bought, or a week for the first
  block.
- Engineers see whether they're ready for client work.
- Engineers who are ready are told that they claim their work from Schedule,
  until they're on their first block.

capabilities.name: Notifications
capabilities.description: People choose which notifications they get and where they go.

decisions.question: Is this the right way to choose notifications?
Which notifications do people want at all?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients, engineers, admins and partners set up the channels their
  notifications can go to, such as the verified email addresses on their
  account.
- Clients are notified when a payment fails, an invoice is issued, or an invited
  member joins.

capabilities.name: Organizations and members
capabilities.description: Clients sign up, create the organization their people share, invite others to it, and give each member a role.

decisions.question: How long is an organization's data kept after it closes?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients log in.
- The software gives a client an engineering team on signing up.
- Clients accept an invitation to join an organization, signing up first if they
  don't have an account yet.
- Clients switch between the organizations they belong to, and create another.
- Clients update the organization's details, and its billing information on the
  payment provider's pages.
- Clients see which partner referred the organization, by name, when one did.
- Admins manage members, and give each one the Admin, Member, or Billing role.
- Admins see the organization's pending invitations, with each one's email
  address, role, and when it was sent.
- Admins revoke a pending invitation.
- Clients leave the organization.

## Success

- Not agreed with the client yet.

capabilities.name: Roles
capabilities.description: Exalynt's admins decide what people may do by making roles: platform roles for people who work with Exalynt, and organization roles for client organizations' members.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins see the permissions roles can grant, and how platform and organization
  roles differ.
- Admins change or delete a platform role, granting each permission at a scope.
- Admins change or delete an organization role, and choose which role whoever
  creates an organization is given.
- Admins start a new role from a copy of another.

capabilities.name: Your profile
capabilities.description: Everyone manages their own account in every app: their name and photo, their email addresses, the accounts they sign in with, their password, and the devices they're signed in on.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Everyone changes their name, and is shown by it everywhere they appear.
- Everyone uploads, changes, or removes their photo, knowing that without one
  their Gravatar shows by default, if their address has one.
- Everyone adds, verifies, and removes email addresses, and makes one primary.
- Everyone connects and disconnects accounts they sign in with, and is told why
  when a provider refuses.
- Everyone sets or resets their password, with a code emailed to them.
- Everyone sees the devices they're signed in on, and signs any other out.

capabilities.name: Agreements
capabilities.description: Admins offer each party the agreement that binds it to Exalynt: a Client Agreement for an organization, an Engineer Agreement for someone working in the console, and a Partner Agreement for a partnership.

decisions.question: When a shared definition changes, how does that reach agreement versions that were already accepted?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins set the Commercial Terms of the Engineer Agreement when inviting
  someone to the console.
- Admins send an engineer a new Engineer Agreement on the terms chosen.
- Admins send an Engineer Agreement with no terms, or no shares.
- Admins see an engineer's Engineer Agreements, offered and accepted, and open
  each accepted one as the PDF made when it was accepted.

capabilities.name: Client agreements
capabilities.description: A client organization's Admin reads and accepts its Client Agreement on its behalf, before anyone can use the portal for it.

decisions.question: When a shared definition changes, how does that reach agreement versions that were already accepted?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Members and Billing see that an Admin has to accept the Client Agreement
  first, and switch to another organization meanwhile.
- Everyone in the organization sees its accepted Client Agreements, who accepted
  each and when, and opens each as the PDF made when it was accepted, to read,
  print, or download.
- Clients are told if another Admin accepted it while they were reading, or
  their role changed so they no longer can, and see the organization as it is
  now instead.

## Success

- Every organization working in the portal has a Client Agreement in effect,
  accepted by one of its Admins without help, and everyone in it can open the
  copy they accepted.

capabilities.name: Engineer agreements
capabilities.description: Engineers read and accept the Engineer Agreement Exalynt sends them, with its Commercial Terms, before they work in the console.

decisions.question: When a shared definition changes, how does that reach agreement versions that were already accepted?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers see their accepted Engineer Agreements, which one is in effect, and
  its terms, and open each accepted one as the PDF made when it was accepted, to
  read, print, or download.
- Engineers see a newer Engineer Agreement waiting for them, read it in full,
  and accept it.
- Engineers are told if the one they're accepting was replaced or already
  accepted while they read it, and read what's waiting now instead.

## Success

- Every engineer working in the console has an Engineer Agreement in effect,
  reads and accepts a new one without help, and is paid by the terms they
  accepted.

capabilities.name: Partner agreements
capabilities.description: A partnership's manager reads and accepts the Partner Agreement Exalynt sends with its invitation, with its Commercial Terms, before working in the Partner Hub for that partnership.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners look at another partnership they manage while one's Partner Agreement
  waits for them.
- Partners see the partnership's Partner Agreements, which one is in effect, and
  open each accepted one as the PDF made when it was accepted, to read, print,
  or download.
- Partners are told if the one they're accepting was accepted elsewhere while
  they read it, and see where it stands instead.
- Admins read any partnership's Partner Agreements, offered and accepted.

## Success

- Every partnership working in the Partner Hub has a Partner Agreement in
  effect, accepted by its manager without help, and its manager can open the
  copy they accepted.

capabilities.name: Billing
capabilities.description: Clients pay for the capacity they buy with their default payment method, and each purchase issues an invoice.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- The payment provider holds each organization's payment methods, billing
  details and invoices, and works out and collects the tax on each invoice from
  the organization's billing address.
- Clients add and remove payment methods, and set a default.
- Clients see the tax on a purchase, as the payment provider works it out,
  before buying, and pay it with the purchase on the same invoice.
- Clients see when a block is pending payment or its payment failed, and pay an
  unpaid invoice.
- Clients view and download invoices and see their payment statuses, on the
  payment provider's pages.
- Admins see purchases, invoices, and their payment statuses.

capabilities.name: Client coupons
capabilities.description: Exalynt's admins give one client a coupon: a name, and a percentage or amount off each block they buy, either forever or on their next purchase.

decisions.question: Is a coupon for one client, taken off each block's price, forever or once, the shape Exalynt needs?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins end a coupon, and see a client's coupons, active, used up, and ended.
- Admins see where each coupon was used, and what it took off.

capabilities.name: Availability
capabilities.description: Engineers set how much of each week they offer, in capacity units, and that adds up per team to decide which weeks have room, though clients never see it directly.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers set a recurring weekly baseline.
- Engineers make a one-off adjustment for a particular week.
- Engineers see their effective availability by week, next to what's assigned or
  scheduled against it, across every client their team supports.
- Engineers see their teammates' availability.
- Engineers reduce their availability. Where that leaves less than a week's
  blocks need, they see which blocks it would take out, and confirm or keep the
  week as it was.
- Engineers change a run of weeks, or the baseline, in one go.
- Team leads see the effective availability, upcoming and current assignments,
  and fulfillment status of their team's engineers.
- Admins set their own weekly baseline and adjust particular weeks, as engineers
  do.

capabilities.name: Capacity purchasing
capabilities.description: Clients buy engineering capacity in blocks, charged at once to their organization's default payment method on one invoice, to schedule now or later.

decisions.question: The site says blocks are "bought after a call, not from a card", but clients can purchase in the app. Does a client's first block, or every block, follow a call? A client can buy before it has a team, and Exalynt contacts a new client before its first block starts, outside the product.

We promise to fulfill or refund every block. When and how a refund happens, who can start one, and whether a client can cancel a block that hasn't been fulfilled are all still open. That includes what happens to unfulfilled blocks when a client closes their account, and whether a refunded first purchase still opens a partnership's earning window.

Each type of block's Capacity Payout Basis is listed with its price for anyone signed in, clients included, so engineers can see what a block would earn them before claiming it. Whether clients should see it, beside the price they pay, is still to be decided.

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients review an order with its tax, as the payment provider works it out,
  before buying it for that total.
- Clients buy more than one block for the same week, to move separate work
  forward in parallel.
- Clients see every block they've bought in one table, sorted by any column and
  filtered by status, type, engineer, team, and when it was bought, each with
  its type, size, who's on it, its week, when it was bought, and what it needs
  from them next.
- Clients open any block to see it on its own, with its invoice.

capabilities.name: Claiming blocks
capabilities.description: Engineers see their weeks on My Schedule beside what their team's clients have scheduled that nobody's on, and claim the blocks that fit their availability, or unclaim one until its week starts.

decisions.question: An engineer can unclaim until a block's week starts, even hours before, leaving it with nobody as the week begins. Keep that, or stop unclaiming some days before the week starts?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers see their upcoming and current blocks, for any client.
- Engineers see their weeks a month at a time, each with their availability and
  the blocks they're on. What doesn't fit their availability shows too, greyed,
  with why.
- Engineers see what each block would earn them once it's fulfilled, by the
  Engineer Share in their agreement and the block's payout basis.
- Engineers see what's expected of them that week before claiming a block.
- Engineers claim a block late, after its preferred week has started.
- Before claiming, engineers see any other block that week the claim would leave
  with nobody who can take it, and can claim anyway.
- Engineers unclaim a block whether they claimed it or an admin put them on it.
  It goes back to the client's shared queue.

capabilities.name: Client directory
capabilities.description: Exalynt's admins see every client organization, the blocks each has bought and how far the work has got, and assign the teams that serve it.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins see how many of each client's blocks aren't fulfilled yet.
- Admins see a client's teams, and unassign them.
- Admins see each of a client's blocks with its week, who's on it, and the
  invoice it was bought on.

capabilities.name: Client home
capabilities.description: Clients land on a page showing what's happening with their capacity, and what's waiting on them.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see their blocks by week, each with the engineer on it, its type, and
  its status: this week's, with any from earlier weeks not finished yet, the
  next three weeks booked, and the last three weeks' completed.
- Clients open any block's own page from there.
- A block whose week passed with no work begun shows as missed, with Exalynt
  rebooking it.
- Clients see how many blocks are at each status, with scheduling what's waiting
  for a week and buying more a step away.
- Clients buy capacity from the top of the page.
- Clients see the capacity booked and how far it reaches, their team, and their
  account.

## Success

- A client opening the portal can tell what's being worked this week, what's
  booked next, and what's waiting on them, without opening another page.

capabilities.name: Conversation spaces
capabilities.description: A client's people and the Exalynt engineers who work with them talk about the work in a space of their own with the messaging provider, in Google Chat outside the app or with Stream inside it, and about each block in conversations they start there, each on a subject of its own.

decisions.question: They're reached by email, outside the app. Whether anything should help with that is undecided.

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- The app keeps who belongs where in step with the messaging provider, and
  points at the conversations.
- Clients join their organization's space once they're in the organization:
  they're put in, or invited if the messaging provider requires it, without
  asking.
- Clients talk about any block from when it's bought.
- Engineers join the space of every client their team supports, without asking.
- Engineers see who is in a client's space: the client's people and Exalynt's,
  which of them leads a team, who has yet to accept an invitation, and who can't
  join and has to be emailed instead.
- Engineers see a block's conversations, how many messages each has, when the
  last came, and how many they haven't read, and open them: in the console with
  Stream, or in Google Chat.
- Team leads do everything an engineer can, for the clients their team supports.
- Admins do everything an engineer can, for every client.

capabilities.name: Engineers
capabilities.description: Exalynt's admins see everyone who works with Exalynt: their team, what they're working on, and whether they're ready for client work.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins see whether someone leads their team.
- Admins see someone's role, when they joined, and the blocks they're on across
  every client.
- Admins see an engineer's availability, whether they can be paid, and whether
  they've written a bio.

capabilities.name: Estimates
capabilities.description: Exalynt prepares estimates of what a project might take, and clients and prospects read them to see what each focus and the project would cost and take on every block type.

decisions.question: Is asking for an estimate, or for a particular engineer, a flow of its own? _At MVP:_ no. Clients ask Exalynt outside the product.

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see the pace each focus of an estimate is planned at, and any
  discounts off it.
- Clients download an estimate as a PDF.
- Engineers prepare and update estimates: focuses, such as new features or
  improvements to an existing system, each sized, planned at a pace and still
  priced on every block type, with an optional description and notes, and
  discounts off the whole project.
- Admins prepare and update estimates for any client organization, or for a
  prospect that isn't a client yet, with discounts off the whole project.
- Admins send a prospect their estimate as a PDF, and attach it to their
  organization once they sign up.

capabilities.name: Fulfillment
capabilities.description: A block's engineer starts it once its week begins, and marks it fulfilled when the work is done, with nobody reviewing it.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers see their blocks on My blocks by where each stands: scheduled, ready
  (its week has started and it isn't started yet), in progress, and fulfilled.
- Engineers open a block they're on and see its client, type, week, focus, size,
  and what it earns them, with its next step.
- Engineers add a focus to a block they're on, saying what its work is about: a
  title, a description, and the client's images, videos (each with a caption if
  they like), and files. Or they search the client's focuses and choose one
  already written, such as one carried over from last week's block.
- Engineers edit a block's focus, which changes it on every block it's on,
  change the block to a different focus, new or existing, or take it off the
  block.
- Engineers post updates on a block they're on as they work: text, metrics
  (before and after), the client's images, videos and files, and links to things
  elsewhere, such as a pull request.
- Engineers edit or delete their updates.
- Engineers see when a block they're on was started and fulfilled, and who
  started it.
- Team leads start their team's engineers' blocks.
- Team leads add, choose, edit, change, or take off the focus of their team's
  engineers' blocks.
- Team leads post, edit, and delete updates on their team's engineers' blocks.
- Admins start any block.
- Admins add, choose, edit, change, or take off the focus of any block.
- Admins post, edit, and delete updates on any block.
- Clients follow each block's status: in progress once it's started, then
  fulfilled.
- Clients open a block on its own page in the portal and read its focus, with
  its images, videos and files, and its updates, beside when it was started and
  fulfilled. That page is a prototype.
- On that page, clients add a focus to any of their blocks, whether or not an
  engineer is on it yet: a title, a description, and images, videos (each with a
  caption if they like), and files they upload. Or they search their focuses and
  choose one already written.
- Clients edit a block's focus, which changes it on every block it's on, change
  the block to a different focus, new or existing, or take it off the block.

capabilities.name: Operations and ownership
capabilities.description: Clients choose whether they or Exalynt operate the software Exalynt builds for them, and keep what they own.

decisions.question: The client chooses how their software is operated and can decide any time before launch. Exalynt operates only software it built.
For software Exalynt operates, the operations fee starts only once it's in production use. Infrastructure is passed through at cost.
A client can take over operations at any time. The handoff is one-way, and Exalynt doesn't take operations back.
The client owns the custom software, its source code, and their data, and keeps them when they stop. Exalynt keeps its reusable libraries, tooling, and frameworks.
Who marks software as live in production, which starts the operations fee?
Who carries out a takeover, and how are source code, data, and deployment and configuration artifacts handed over?
Who records infrastructure pass-through charges, and how often are they billed?
Operations needs fleshing out as a whole. Client capabilities and rules are written, but Exalynt's side isn't decided yet.

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see whether each piece of their software is live in production, and
  whether it's **Self Operated** or **Operated by Exalynt**.
- Clients take over operations of software Exalynt operates, and receive its
  source code, data, and deployment and configuration artifacts.
- Clients get their source code and data at any time, including when they stop
  working with Exalynt.
- Clients see where their code lives and who has access to it.

capabilities.name: Scheduling
capabilities.description: Clients schedule each block into a week that has room, against what the engineers on their organization's teams offer, and can move it to another week, or take it back out, until that week starts.

decisions.question: Until when can a client move or take back a scheduled block? Any time before its week starts, or only up to some point before it?
Do clients get reminders to schedule? Can admins or leads schedule on a client's behalf? What happens to capacity that's never scheduled?
Is a reason shown to the client? Should moving the week of a block that has an assigned engineer require someone to acknowledge coverage?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see each block's preferred week, its assigned engineer if there is
  one, and that engineer's team.
- The software takes an engineer off a block the client takes back out of its
  week.
- Admins move a block's preferred week.

capabilities.name: Staffing
capabilities.description: Each scheduled block gets one engineer: an eligible engineer claims it from the client's shared queue, as [Claiming blocks](claiming-blocks.md) covers, or an admin assigns it.

decisions.question: Do leads confirm a handoff in the product, or coordinate outside the product and have the current engineer release the block?
Are there reminders before the preferred week starts, and who owns escalation once a block is urgent? Which channels carry release and urgent alerts?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Admins see capacity purchases, and upcoming and current assignments, across
  all clients and teams.
- Admins spot overbooked blocks, and blocks that are scheduled but unassigned.
- Admins reassign or unassign a scheduled block.

capabilities.name: Teams
capabilities.description: Exalynt groups its people into teams to work with the clients they're assigned to, and a client's teams decide who at Exalynt it sees.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Clients see the engineering teams assigned to their organization, and each
  team's engineers and lead.
- Clients get to know each engineer on their teams through their short bio, and
  see how long they've been with Exalynt.
- Engineers see the team they belong to, its members, and its lead if there is
  one.
- Engineers see which clients their team supports.
- Engineers see their teammates' bios.
- Engineers write a bio about themselves, and change or clear it.
- Team leads see the team they lead, its engineers, and the clients it supports.
- Admins invite an engineer to Exalynt by email, including someone who already
  has an account as a client member or partner.
- Admins see pending engineer invitations, with each one's email address and
  when it was sent, and revoke one.
- Admins choose the team an engineer joins when they accept their invitation.
- Admins write, change, or clear any engineer's bio.
- Admins create and manage engineering teams.
- Admins assign an engineer to a team, move them to another team, or remove them
  from their team.
- Admins designate or remove a team's lead.
- Admins assign engineering teams to a client organization, or remove them.

capabilities.name: Client invitations
capabilities.description: Partners invite people they know to become Exalynt clients by email, and each one who signs up as a new client is attributed to their partnership.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners see the invitations the partnership has sent, newest first, and
  whether each has signed up.
- Partners resend an invitation, or revoke it.
- Partners are told when the partnership has sent as many new invitations as it
  can in a day, 50, or an invitation was sent too recently to resend, and when
  to try again.
- Clients sign up from a partner's email invitation, and are told when signing
  up that the partner may earn from it.

## Success

- Partners invite people they know by email without help, and each one who signs
  up as a new client is attributed to the partnership that invited them.

capabilities.name: Partner clients
capabilities.description: Partners see the clients attributed to their partnership: who they are, how each came to it, since when, and how long the partnership earns on each.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners see the most recently attributed clients first, and how each came to
  them: their referral code, their invitation, or Exalynt.
- Partners see the latest clients at a glance where they land in the Partner
  Hub, and go on to all of them.

## Success

- Every partner sees, without asking Exalynt, which clients are attributed to
  their partnership, how each came, and how long it earns on each.

capabilities.name: Partner home
capabilities.description: Partners land on the partnership they manage at a glance, with the clients it has brought in, how to bring in more, and how it earns.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners see the partnership's name and when it enrolled, and rename it.
- Partners see its latest clients, each with how it came to them and since when,
  and go on to all of them.
- Partners copy its referral code and sign-up link, or go on to invite someone
  by email.
- Partners see its terms, and what each kind of block earns on them: its share
  of that block's capacity payout basis.
- Partners are told when the partnership has no payout account to be paid into.
- Partners see what the partnership has earned, what's waiting to be paid out,
  and what's bought but not earned yet.

capabilities.name: Partnerships
capabilities.description: Partners Exalynt has enrolled each manage a partnership, and introduce people to Exalynt by giving them its referral code or inviting them by email.

decisions.question: Can a partner get a new code, for instance after sharing one too widely, and does the old one stop working?
Terms are set when inviting a partnership. Can an admin change them afterwards, and if so, does a change reach clients already attributed or only those attributed after it?

capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Exalynt enrolls clients, engineers, or established external partners.
- Clients sign up with a partner's referral code or link, and are told when
  signing up that the partner may earn from it.
- Partners accept Exalynt's invitation to the Partnership Program and its
  Partner Agreement in one step, reading the agreement first.
- Partners name the partnership after themselves or the business they partner
  for, and rename it.
- Partners see and copy the partnership's referral code and sign-up link, with a
  reminder to tell the people they share it with that they may earn from it.
- Partners see the partnership's terms: its share, what it's a share of, and how
  long it earns on each client, or that it has no time limit.
- Partners who manage several partnerships switch between them, viewing one at a
  time.
- Admins enroll a partner in the Partnership Program by inviting them by email,
  including someone who already has an account as a client member or engineer,
  and see any partnerships they already manage.
- Admins set a partnership's terms when inviting it, as its Partner Agreement's
  Commercial Terms, the same way as an engineer's: its Referral Share and its
  Earning Window, how long it earns on each client, or no time limit, starting
  from 5% of the engineering capacity referred clients purchase and have
  fulfilled within 12 months. Inviting with no Referral Share, or no terms at
  all, asks the admin to confirm first, since the partnership then earns
  nothing.
- Admins see pending partner invitations, with each one's email address, the
  partnership it's for, and when it was sent, and revoke one.
- Admins see the clients attributed to each partnership, with how each came to
  it and since when.
- Admins attribute a client to a partnership, which moves it from any other, and
  remove a client's attribution.
- Admins see each partnership's terms, and each of its clients' earning windows.
- Admins see what a partnership has earned, in total and on each client, block
  by block, and every payout sent to it.

capabilities.name: Earnings
capabilities.description: People see what they earn on each block, from when it's assigned to when it's fulfilled.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers see earnings from their blocks, with each block's client, amount,
  whether it's earned yet, payout status, and payment history.
- Engineers see the team support they've earned, and whose block each share came
  from.
- Team leads see the blocks their team's engineers have fulfilled, with each
  block's engineer, client, and payout status.
- Team leads see their team-lead earnings separately from their own engineering
  earnings, even when both go to the same payout account.
- Team leads see which fulfilled blocks created their share.

capabilities.name: Partner earnings
capabilities.description: Partners see what their partnership earns on each of its clients' blocks: what each block has earned or will, how long each client's earning window has left, and what's waiting to be paid.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners see every block the partnership's clients bought within their earning
  windows, the most recently bought first: its client, type, when it was bought,
  its capacity payout basis and the partnership's percentage of it, the amount,
  and whether that's not earned yet, waiting, on hold, on its way, or paid.
- While a block isn't earned yet, partners see whether it's scheduled, and for
  which week.
- Partners see totals, on their phone as well: what the partnership has earned
  and how much of it is paid, what's waiting to be paid out, and what's bought
  but not earned yet.
- Partners are told why earned earnings are on hold, when the partnership's
  payout account can't be paid yet.

## Success

- Every partner sees, without asking Exalynt, what their partnership has earned
  on each client's blocks, what's waiting to be paid, and what's bought but not
  earned yet.

capabilities.name: Partner payout accounts
capabilities.description: Partners set up and look after the one bank account each partnership they manage is paid to, its own apart from theirs and any other partnership's.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners set up the payout account on the payments partner's form, telling it
  whether the partnership is paid as a person or a business.
- Partners see whether it can be paid, and what to fix if it can't, and fix it
  on the same form.
- Partners change the bank account, or remove it.
- Partners see that the partnership's earnings are held until it has one that
  can be paid, in the Partner Hub's setup steps and on its pages.

## Success

- Every partnership manager sets up, fixes, or removes the partnership's own
  payout account on their own, and can tell whether it can be paid.

capabilities.name: Partner payouts
capabilities.description: Each partnership is paid what it earns into its own payout account, never its manager's, once an admin releases it, and its manager sees each payout.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Partners see every payout sent to the partnership, newest first: when it was
  sent, the bank account it went to, whether it arrived, and the blocks it paid,
  each with its client, basis, percentage and amount as they were when it was
  sent.
- Partners see why a payout failed, and when it was sent again.

## Success

- Every partnership is paid what it earns into its own account each week an
  admin releases, and its manager sees each payout and what it carried without
  asking Exalynt.

capabilities.name: Payout accounts
capabilities.description: People and partnerships each have one bank account their payouts go to, which they add, change, fix, remove, and see whether it can be paid.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers add the bank account their payouts go to on the payments partner's
  form, and see what to fix if it can't be paid.

capabilities.name: Payouts
capabilities.description: Admins release what people and partnerships have earned, and it goes to each payee's payout account.
capabilities.body:
## Includes

- Engineers see earnings waiting for a payout, and earnings on hold, with what
  they need to fix.
- Engineers see every payout they've been sent, what it was made up of, and
  where it went.
- Engineers see why a payout failed, and the payout it was sent again as.
- Admins see what's waiting to be released, by payee, a person or a partnership,
  with what each line is for.
- Admins see whose earnings are on hold, and why.
- Admins see failed payouts, why each failed, and whether it's been sent again.
- Admins see past releases.

rules.name: Adding a hat to an account
rules.body: To add a hat to an existing account, invite the address that account uses.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who takes on another hat keeps their one account, and gains what the new hat needs alongside what they had

rules.name: Gaining a hat takes nothing away
rules.body:
Gaining a hat never takes another away, and each keeps its own rules. Being a
partner doesn't change an engineer's share or team.

verifies.text: Rule: Gaining a hat never takes another away

rules.name: Invitations go to an email address
rules.body:
Invitations are sent to an email address, and the invitee accepts signed in
with that address. Someone without an account signs up with it first.

verifies.text: Rule: An invitation to an organization is accepted only by the person it was sent to, signed in with that address
Rule: Accepting an invitation makes the invitee a member, with the role they were invited to, and it's no longer pending

rules.name: Invitations stay pending until resolved
rules.body:
An invitation stays pending until it's accepted or revoked, and doesn't expire.
A revoked invitation can't be accepted, and an accepted one is no longer
pending.

verifies.text: Rule: An invitation stays pending until it's accepted or revoked, and doesn't expire
Rule: Accepting an invitation makes the invitee a member, with the role they were invited to, and it's no longer pending
Rule: A revoked invitation is no longer pending for the invitee and can't be accepted

rules.name: One account, however many hats
rules.body:
A person has one account, however many hats they wear. Someone who already has
an account and takes on another persona keeps that account and gains the apps
and functions the new one needs, alongside what they already have. An engineer
invited to be a partner gains the Partner Hub. A client member invited to be an
engineer gains the console. An engineer who signs up as a client creates an
organization from the account they already have.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who takes on another hat keeps their one account, and gains what the new hat needs alongside what they had
Rule: Creating an organization gives its creator the portal, alongside the applications they already had

rules.name: Who sees and revokes pending invitations
rules.body: Whoever can send an invitation can see it while it's pending, or revoke it.

verifies.text: Rule: Only a client Admin sees or revokes the organization's invitations

rules.name: Billing and member notifications follow role
rules.body:
In a client organization, billing notifications go only to members whose role
can see billing, and member notifications only to those who can manage members.

rules.name: Choices are private
rules.body:
Each person's choices are their own. Nobody else can see or change them, admins
included.

rules.name: Each app offers its own notifications
rules.body:
Each app offers only the notifications for who someone is in it: the portal a
client's, the console an engineer's and a team lead's, the admin an admin's,
and the Partner Hub a partner's. A notification offered in more than one app
has one setting, shared across them.

rules.name: Email only to verified addresses
rules.body:
Email goes only to a verified address on the person's account, the one they
chose for that notification or else their first.

rules.name: Lost access stops notifications
rules.body:
Someone who loses access to an organization, team, or partnership stops being
told about it, and keeps their choices.

rules.name: Nobody hears of their own actions
rules.body: Nobody is told about something they did themselves.

rules.name: Notifications respect what someone can see
rules.body:
Nobody is told about anything they couldn't otherwise see. A notification about
an organization's work goes only to its members, the teams assigned to it, and
Exalynt staff.

rules.name: One set of choices across organizations
rules.body:
One set of choices covers every organization someone belongs to, and each
notification names the organization it's about.

rules.name: Payout release reminders
rules.body:
An admin is told when payouts are ready to release, and again if they're still
waiting to be released.

rules.name: Recipients choose the channels
rules.body:
A notification goes only to the channels its recipient chose for it, and to at
least one while it's on.

rules.name: Removed addresses stop email immediately
rules.body:
Removing a verified address from an account stops email going to it at once,
whatever had been chosen.

rules.name: Removed channels fall back to others
rules.body:
When a channel or address is removed, the notifications that used it go to the
person's remaining channels. Their last channel can't be removed.

rules.name: Some notifications can't be turned off
rules.body:
Some notifications can't be turned off: a moved preferred week, a failed
payment, and a payout account that needs attention. The person still chooses
which channel they go to.

rules.name: Turned-off notifications aren't sent
rules.body: A notification someone has turned off isn't sent to them.

rules.name: What admins are told
rules.body:
An admin is told when an organization signs up, an engineer or partner accepts
an invitation, capacity is purchased, a block has no engineer when its week
starts, a week is overbooked, a client's payment fails, a payout fails, an
engineer lacks a valid payout account, or a referral code attributes a client.

rules.name: What clients are told
rules.body:
A client is told when an engineer is assigned to or comes off a block, a block
has no engineer when its week starts, Exalynt moves a preferred week, a block
is fulfilled, an estimate is ready, or a team is assigned or removed.

rules.name: What engineers are told
rules.body:
An engineer is told when a block joins their team's queue, they're put on or
taken off a block, its week starts, they change teams or their team's clients
change, a payout is sent, or their payout account needs attention.

rules.name: What partners are told
rules.body:
A partner is told when a referred client signs up or first purchases, an
earning window is closing, an admin changes an attribution, a share is earned,
a payout is sent or fails, or their payout account needs setting up.

rules.name: What team leads are also told
rules.body:
A team lead is also told when an engineer joins or leaves their team or becomes
ineligible.

rules.name: Deleted objects can't be found
rules.body: Once an object is deleted, neither it nor its content can be found.

rules.name: Listing positions belong to one organization
rules.body: A listing position only works for the organization it came from.

rules.name: Objects stay within their organization
rules.body: Another organization can't reach a client's objects.

verifies.text: Rule: Another organization can't reach a client's objects

rules.name: Upload types and file names
rules.body:
An upload sent as generic bytes takes the type its bytes suggest, and its file
name is reduced to its base name, with no directories.

rules.name: Admins see and revoke all invitations
rules.body:
Every admin sees and revokes all of Exalynt's pending invitations, not only the
ones they sent. A revoked invitation can't be accepted.

rules.name: Engineers join by invitation only
rules.body:
Engineers join only by an admin's invitation. There's no self sign-up as an
engineer.

rules.name: Existing accounts gain the engineer role
rules.body:
Someone who already has an account, such as a client member or a partner,
accepts an engineer invitation with that account and gains the engineer role
and the console alongside what they already have, rather than a second account.

rules.name: Invalid payout accounts delay payment
rules.body:
Shares from blocks fulfilled while an engineer's payout account isn't valid are
still earned, and are paid once the account is valid again.

rules.name: Invited engineers join their team
rules.body: An engineer invited onto a team joins it on accepting.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer invited onto a team joins it on accepting

rules.name: When an engineer is ready
rules.body:
An engineer is ready for client work once they have set their availability and
are on a team. A bio and a payout account are recommended, and don't stop them
being ready.

rules.name: Personal things follow the person
rules.body: What belongs to a person works wherever they act.

verifies.text: Rule: What belongs to a person works wherever they act

rules.name: Team rooms are shared across clients
rules.body: A team's room is shared by the clients it supports.

verifies.text: Rule: A team's room is shared by the clients it supports

rules.name: Accepting makes someone a member
rules.body:
Accepting an invitation makes the invitee a member of the organization, listed
with their email address and the role they were invited to, and the
organization appears among theirs. Once accepted, the invitation is no longer
pending for them.

verifies.text: Rule: Accepting an invitation makes the invitee a member, with the role they were invited to, and it's no longer pending

rules.name: Admins alone see and revoke invitations
rules.body:
Only a client Admin sees or revokes the organization's invitations, as with
managing members.

verifies.text: Rule: Only a client Admin sees or revokes the organization's invitations

rules.name: Anyone can create an organization
rules.body:
Anyone can sign up as a client and create an organization, without an
invitation. Someone who already has an account, such as an engineer or a
partner, creates their organization from that account rather than a new one.

verifies.text: Rule: Creating an organization gives its creator the portal, alongside the applications they already had
Rule: A new organization's creator holds the role given to creators

rules.name: Anyone can leave, not remove others
rules.body:
A member who can't manage members can't remove anyone else, but can remove
themselves, leaving the organization.

verifies.text: Rule: A member who can't manage members can't remove anyone else, but can remove themselves, leaving the organization

rules.name: Billing members handle only billing
rules.body:
A client's Billing member sees invoices, pays them, and manages payment
methods. Beyond that, they don't work with capacity, scheduling, or members.

verifies.text: Rule: A client's Billing member sees invoices, pays them, and manages payment methods, and doesn't work with capacity, scheduling, or members

rules.name: Client Admins run the organization
rules.body: A client Admin runs the organization: capacity, billing, and members.

verifies.text: Rule: A client Admin runs the organization: capacity, billing, and members

rules.name: Client Members see payment state, not invoices
rules.body:
A client Member can see whether a block is pending payment or its payment
failed. They don't see invoices or amounts.

verifies.text: Rule: A client Member can see whether a block is pending payment or its payment failed, but not its invoice

rules.name: Client Members work without billing
rules.body: A client Member schedules capacity, but can't purchase capacity or see billing.

verifies.text: Rule: A client Member schedules capacity, but can't purchase capacity or see billing

rules.name: Creators get client access
rules.body:
Creating an organization gives its creator the portal, alongside the
applications they already had.

verifies.text: Rule: Creating an organization gives its creator the portal, alongside the applications they already had

rules.name: Former members can rejoin
rules.body: Someone who left an organization can be invited again and rejoin it.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who left an organization can be invited again and rejoin it

rules.name: Giving up member management
rules.body:
Once another member holds a role that can manage members, a member can give up
their own ability to manage members.

verifies.text: Rule: Once another member holds a role that can manage members, a member can give up their own ability to manage members

rules.name: Invitations are limited
rules.body:
An organization can send at most 50 invitations in a day, and so can each
person, across every organization they invite people to. Revoking one, or its
being accepted, doesn't free up another. So nobody is flooded with email from
Exalynt, even by someone who signs up just to send it.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization, and each person, can send at most 50 invitations a day, and revoking one doesn't free up another

rules.name: Invitations carry organization roles only
rules.body:
An organization invitation only goes to an organization role, never a platform
role.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization invitation only goes to an organization role, never a platform role

rules.name: Leaving ends access
rules.body: Someone who has left an organization can no longer act in it.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who has left an organization can no longer act in it

rules.name: Logos must be raster images
rules.body: A logo must be a raster image, so an SVG is refused.

verifies.text: Rule: A logo must be a raster image, so an SVG is refused

rules.name: Logos stay within their organization
rules.body: A client can't reach another organization's logo.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can't reach another organization's logo

rules.name: Members act only in their organizations
rules.body: Someone may act only in an organization they belong to.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone may act only in an organization they belong to

rules.name: New members hold their role's permissions
rules.body:
Acting in the organization, a new member holds exactly their role's
permissions, and has the portal.

verifies.text: Rule: Acting in the organization, a new member holds exactly their role's permissions, and has the portal

rules.name: Newcomers start with no organization
rules.body:
Someone newly signed up belongs to no organization until they create one, and
then it's the only one they see.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone newly signed up belongs to no organization until they create one, and then it's the only one they see

rules.name: One pending invitation per person
rules.body:
Someone can't be invited to an organization twice while an invitation to them
is pending, whatever the case of their email address, and the organization
lists the one invitation.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone can't be invited to an organization twice while an invitation to them is pending, whatever the case of their email address

rules.name: Only Admins purchase or manage members
rules.body: Only a client Admin can purchase capacity or manage members.

verifies.text: Rule: Only a client Admin can purchase capacity or manage members

rules.name: Only the invitee can accept
rules.body:
An invitation to an organization is accepted signed in with the email address
it was sent to, and only the person invited can accept it; anyone else finds
nothing. Someone who already has an account joins with it.

verifies.text: Rule: What belongs to a person works wherever they act
Rule: An invitation to an organization is accepted only by the person it was sent to, signed in with that address

rules.name: Organization listings show logo status
rules.body:
An organization's listing shows whether it has a logo, and that changes when
the logo is set or removed. Once a logo is removed, it can no longer be
downloaded.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization's listing shows whether it has a logo, and a removed logo can no longer be downloaded

rules.name: Organization-only actions need an organization
rules.body:
Something that can only be done in an organization is refused when no
organization is named.

verifies.text: Rule: What someone may do follows where they act

rules.name: Organizations start without a logo
rules.body: An organization has no logo until one is set.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization has no logo until one is set

rules.name: Outsiders can't rename an organization
rules.body: Someone outside an organization can't rename it.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone outside an organization can't rename it

rules.name: Revoked invitations can't be accepted
rules.body:
A revoked invitation is no longer pending for the invitee and can't be
accepted.

verifies.text: Rule: A revoked invitation is no longer pending for the invitee and can't be accepted

rules.name: Someone always manages members
rules.body:
An organization always has at least one member who can manage members, such as
an Admin. The last one can't be removed, leave, or be given a role that can't
manage members, including by changing their own role. So an organization's last
member can't be removed either.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization always has at least one member who can manage members

rules.name: Everyone sees the uploaded photo
rules.body: The photo someone uploads is the one everyone who sees them sees.

verifies.text: Rule: The photo someone uploads is the one everyone who sees them sees

rules.name: Removed photos are no longer shown
rules.body: Someone who removes their photo is shown without one.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who removes their photo is shown without one

rules.body:
Someone keeps at least a first or last name. The profile page enforces it, so
its unit tests check it, not this suite.

rules.name: Everyone sees the name given
rules.body: The name someone gives is the one everyone who sees them sees.

verifies.text: Rule: The name someone gives is the one everyone who sees them sees

rules.name: Invitations follow the primary address
rules.body: An invitation goes by the address someone has made primary.

verifies.text: Rule: An invitation goes by the address someone has made primary

rules.name: Accepting an invitation to Exalynt
rules.body:
Accepting an invitation to work with Exalynt gives the invitee the platform
role, its permissions, and the applications they were invited to, and the
invitation leaves Exalynt's pending invitations.

rules.name: Acting as engineer or client, never both
rules.body:
Someone who is both an engineer and a client member acts as one or the other,
never both.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone who is both an engineer and a client member acts as one or the other, never both

rules.name: Applications show on the person
rules.body: The applications set for someone show on that person, listed in order.

rules.name: Creators get the creator role
rules.body: A new organization's creator holds the role given to creators.

verifies.text: Rule: A new organization's creator holds the role given to creators

rules.name: Deleted roles can't be found
rules.body: Once a role is deleted, it can't be found.

verifies.text: Rule: Once a role is deleted, it can't be found

rules.name: Exalynt invitations show as pending
rules.body:
An invitation to work with Exalynt shows as pending for the invitee, as an
invitation to no organization, naming the platform role.

rules.name: Exalynt-only permissions can't be granted
rules.body: Nobody can grant what only Exalynt's own systems hold.

verifies.text: Rule: Nobody can grant what only Exalynt's own systems hold

rules.name: Held organization roles can't be deleted
rules.body: An organization role someone holds can't be deleted.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization role someone holds can't be deleted

rules.name: Held platform roles can't be deleted
rules.body: A platform role someone holds can't be deleted.

verifies.text: Rule: A platform role someone holds can't be deleted

rules.name: Held roles keep member management
rules.body: An organization role someone holds keeps the ability to manage members.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization role someone holds keeps the ability to manage members

rules.name: Invited roles can't be deleted
rules.body: A role someone has been invited to can't be deleted.

verifies.text: Rule: A role someone has been invited to can't be deleted

rules.name: Inviting with applications needs access
rules.body:
Someone who only gives out platform roles can't invite someone with
applications.

rules.name: Listing people requires a platform role
rules.body: Someone with no platform role can't list people.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone with no platform role can't list people

rules.name: Member permissions follow their role
rules.body: A member's permissions follow their role.

verifies.text: Rule: A member's permissions follow their role

rules.name: New people have no applications
rules.body: A new person has no applications.

rules.name: No platform role means no permissions
rules.body: Acting in no organization, someone with no platform role holds no permissions.

verifies.text: Rule: Acting in no organization, someone with no platform role holds no permissions
Rule: Only Exalynt lists its clients

rules.name: Only one creator role
rules.body: Only one organization role is given to creators.

verifies.text: Rule: Only one organization role is given to creators

rules.name: Outsiders can't change organization roles
rules.body: Someone can't change roles in an organization they don't belong to.

verifies.text: Rule: Someone can't change roles in an organization they don't belong to

rules.name: Own-scoped capacity access
rules.body:
An engineer allowed to read capacity only at their own scope sees only the
blocks they're staffed on.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer allowed to read capacity only at their own scope sees only the blocks they're staffed on

rules.name: People lists exclude clients
rules.body:
Acting in no organization, the people listed are only those who work with
Exalynt, holding a platform role, never clients.

verifies.text: Rule: Acting in no organization, the people listed are only those who work with Exalynt, holding a platform role, never clients

rules.name: Permissions follow where someone acts
rules.body: What someone may do follows where they act.

verifies.text: Rule: What someone may do follows where they act

rules.name: Platform roles aren't organization roles
rules.body:
A platform role is not an organization role, and looking for it as one finds
nothing.

rules.name: Platform roles can be taken away
rules.body: An administrator can take away someone's platform role, leaving them with none.

rules.name: Read-only engineers can't staff blocks
rules.body: An engineer who can only read can't staff a block.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer who can only read can't staff a block

rules.name: Role edits keep the description
rules.body:
Changing a role's name and grants leaves its description as it was, and its
grants are listed by permission.

rules.name: Role names are unique within their kind
rules.body: Role names are unique among their kind, ignoring case.

verifies.text: Rule: Role names are unique among their kind, ignoring case

rules.name: Roles grant only what their kind allows
rules.body: A role only grants what its kind may grant.

verifies.text: Rule: A role only grants what its kind may grant

rules.name: Roles stay with their own kind
rules.body:
An organization role can't be given to someone as their platform role, and a
platform role can't be given to an organization member.

rules.name: Team-scoped capacity access
rules.body:
An engineer allowed to read capacity at team scope sees only what their team
supports.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer allowed to read capacity at team scope sees only what their team supports

rules.name: The creator role can manage members
rules.body: The role given to creators can manage members.

verifies.text: Rule: The role given to creators can manage members

rules.name: What each role kind may grant
rules.body: What each kind of role may grant.

verifies.text: Rule: What each kind of role may grant

rules.name: Who gives out platform roles
rules.body: Only someone who manages people's roles gives out platform roles.

verifies.text: Rule: Only someone who manages people's roles gives out platform roles

rules.name: Who invites people to Exalynt
rules.body:
Only someone who gives out platform roles invites people to work with Exalynt.
A client can't.

rules.name: Who reads permissions and makes roles
rules.body:
Only someone who manages roles reads the permissions roles can grant, or makes
roles.

verifies.text: Rule: Only someone who manages roles reads the permissions roles can grant, or makes roles

rules.name: Who sets application access
rules.body:
Only someone who manages application access sets which applications someone
has. Neither a client nor someone who only gives out platform roles can.

rules.name: A new organization is offered the Client Agreement
rules.body: An organization is offered the Client Agreement when it's created.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization is offered the Client Agreement when it's created

rules.name: A newer agreement replaces one waiting
rules.body:
A newer agreement sent to a party replaces one still waiting for them, so at
most one waits at a time.

verifies.text: Rule: A newer agreement replaces one still waiting

rules.name: Acceptance puts an agreement in effect
rules.body:
An agreement is in effect only once accepted, and the latest accepted
supersedes any before it.

verifies.text: Rule: An agreement is in effect only once accepted, and the latest accepted supersedes any before it

rules.name: Accepted agreements never change
rules.body:
An accepted agreement is kept exactly as accepted, and never changes
afterwards.

verifies.text: Rule: Accepted agreements never change

rules.name: Accepted agreements outlive their party's account
rules.body:
An accepted agreement is kept, as accepted, after its party's account is
deleted.

verifies.text: Rule: An accepted agreement outlives its party's account

rules.name: Agreements stay private
rules.body:
One organization never sees another's agreements, one partnership never sees
another's, and an engineer sees only their own.

verifies.text: Rule: Agreements stay private

rules.name: An Engineer Agreement can have no Commercial Terms
rules.body:
An admin can send an Engineer Agreement with no Commercial Terms, whether with
an invitation or later. The engineer then earns nothing (see [Unlisted shares
earn nothing](../../../pay/rules/earnings-and-payouts)), and the admin confirms
that before sending.

verifies.text: Rule: An admin can send an Engineer Agreement with no Commercial Terms

rules.name: Engineer Agreement follows the invitation's terms
rules.body:
An engineer is offered the Engineer Agreement on the terms their invitation
set.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer is offered the Engineer Agreement on the terms their invitation set

rules.name: Manager accepts the Partner Agreement
rules.body:
A partnership's Partner Agreement is accepted by its manager, and by nobody
else: not another partnership's manager, and not an Exalynt admin, who can only
read it.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership's Partner Agreement is accepted by its manager

rules.name: New terms wait for acceptance
rules.body:
New terms hold only once accepted; until then the agreement in effect keeps its
own.

verifies.text: Rule: New terms hold only once accepted; until then the agreement in effect keeps its own

rules.name: Only the waiting agreement is accepted, once
rules.body:
Only the agreement waiting for a party can be accepted, and only once: one that
was replaced, or is already accepted, can't be.

verifies.text: Rule: Only the waiting agreement can be accepted, and only once

rules.name: Reading the Partner Agreement before accepting
rules.body:
An invited partner can read the Partner Agreement before accepting, and only
the address invited can.

verifies.text: Rule: An invited partner can read the Partner Agreement before accepting, and only the address invited can

rules.name: Who accepts a Client Agreement
rules.body:
An organization's Client Agreement is accepted for it by someone whose role can
manage it.

verifies.text: Rule: An organization's Client Agreement is accepted for it by someone whose role can manage it

rules.name: A changed total buys nothing
rules.body:
A purchase whose total changed since it was quoted buys nothing and owes
nothing, so a client is never charged other than what they were shown.

verifies.text: Rule: A purchase whose total changed since it was quoted buys nothing and owes nothing

rules.name: At most 20 blocks per purchase
rules.body: At most 20 blocks can be bought at once.

verifies.text: Rule: At most 20 blocks can be bought at once

rules.name: Buying charges at once
rules.body: Buying charges the default payment method at once, on one invoice.

verifies.text: Rule: Buying charges the default payment method at once, on one invoice

rules.name: Buying requires a payment method
rules.body: Capacity can't be bought without a payment method.

verifies.text: Rule: Capacity can't be bought without a payment method

rules.name: Capacity, fees, and infrastructure billed separately
rules.body:
Capacity, the operations fee, and infrastructure are billed separately and
never bundled. Only capacity is invoiced today.

rules.name: Company details stay untouched
rules.body: Company details entered with the payment provider stay as the client left them.

verifies.text: Rule: Company details entered with the payment provider stay as the client left them

rules.name: Declined purchases buy nothing
rules.body: A declined purchase buys nothing and owes nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A declined purchase buys nothing and owes nothing

rules.name: Organizations' billing stays separate
rules.body: A client can't see or act on another organization's billing.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can't see or act on another organization's billing

rules.name: Paying an invoice releases its capacity
rules.body: Unpaid capacity becomes usable once its invoice is paid.

verifies.text: Rule: Unpaid capacity becomes usable once its invoice is paid

rules.name: Purchases are quoted with their tax
rules.body: A purchase is quoted with its tax before it's bought, and quoting buys nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A purchase is quoted with its tax before it's bought, and quoting buys nothing

rules.name: Tax needs to know where the client is
rules.body:
Capacity can't be bought or quoted unless the payment provider can tell where
the client is for tax, which takes a billing address it can place.

verifies.text: Rule: Capacity can't be bought or quoted unless the payment provider can tell where the client is for tax

rules.name: The payment provider works out the tax
rules.why: Exalynt is responsible for making sure sales tax is collected, but not for calculating it; the provider holds the billing address and the tax settings it needs.
rules.body:
The payment provider works out a purchase's tax, and it's charged on the
invoice. Exalynt never calculates tax itself.

verifies.text: Rule: The payment provider works out a purchase's tax, and it's charged on the invoice

rules.name: Unpaid invoices are paid with the provider
rules.body: An unpaid invoice is paid at the payment provider's current page for it.

verifies.text: Rule: An unpaid invoice is paid at the payment provider's current page for it

rules.name: When company details count as given
rules.body:
Company details count as given once the payment provider holds the client's
address.

verifies.text: Rule: Company details count as given once the payment provider holds the client's address

rules.name: Who manages billing
rules.body:
Admins and Billing members manage billing on the payment provider's pages;
Members don't.

verifies.text: Rule: Admins and Billing members manage billing on the payment provider's pages; Members don't

rules.name: Adjustments never overlap
rules.body: An engineer's adjustments never cover the same week.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer's adjustments never cover the same week

rules.name: Admins set their own availability
rules.body: Admins set their own availability, as engineers do.

verifies.text: Rule: Admins set their own availability, as engineers do

rules.name: Availability comes in quarter weeks
rules.body: Availability is offered in whole weeks, in quarters of a week.

verifies.text: Rule: Availability is offered in whole weeks, in quarters of a week

rules.name: How a week's availability is decided
rules.body:
A week's availability is the engineer's adjustment for it, otherwise their
baseline once it has started, otherwise nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A week's availability is the engineer's adjustment for it, otherwise their baseline once it has started, otherwise nothing

rules.name: One baseline per engineer
rules.body: An engineer has one baseline.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer has one baseline

rules.name: Only its owner sets availability
rules.body: Nobody sets anyone else's availability.

verifies.text: Rule: Nobody sets anyone else's availability

rules.name: Past weeks can't change
rules.body: Weeks that have gone by can't be changed.

verifies.text: Rule: Weeks that have gone by can't be changed

rules.name: Reductions make room by taking blocks out
rules.why: A week is never overbooked, and clients keep their place in a week wherever a teammate can still fit them.
rules.body:
A reduction that leaves too little room for what's already booked takes blocks
out until it fits, and only once the engineer has seen which blocks those are
and confirmed. The engineer's own blocks that no longer fit their week come off
them first, staying in their week for a teammate to claim. Only if their team's
room is still short are blocks unscheduled, back to their clients to schedule
again.

verifies.text: Rule: A reduction that leaves too little room takes blocks out

rules.name: Reductions need no approval
rules.body: An engineer's reduction of their availability takes effect without approval.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer's reduction of their availability takes effect without approval

rules.name: Reductions never touch started work
rules.body:
A reduction never takes out a block whose week has started or that work has
begun on. A reduction that can't fit without doing so is refused.

verifies.text: Rule: A reduction never takes out work that has started

rules.name: Removing an adjustment restores the baseline
rules.body: Removing an adjustment returns its weeks to the baseline.

verifies.text: Rule: Removing an adjustment returns its weeks to the baseline

rules.name: Who sees an engineer's availability
rules.body: An engineer's availability is seen by them, their team, and admins.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer's availability is seen by them, their team, and admins

rules.name: Block numbers are per organization
rules.body: Blocks are numbered in turn within each organization, and keep their number.

verifies.text: Rule: Blocks are numbered in turn within each organization, and keep their number

rules.name: Blocks are bought, then scheduled
rules.body: A block is bought, then scheduled, and waits in no week until it is.

verifies.text: Rule: A block is bought, then scheduled

rules.name: Blocks stay within their organization
rules.body: A client can't reach another organization's blocks.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can't reach another organization's blocks

rules.name: Buying before having a team
rules.body:
A client can buy before it has a team, and its blocks wait until it can
schedule them.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can buy before it has a team, and its blocks wait until it can schedule them

rules.name: Buying only defined capacity types
rules.body: A client can only buy a defined capacity type.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can only buy a defined capacity type

rules.name: Capacity is never shown as hours
rules.body:
Capacity is shown in blocks and units, never as hours spent, reserved or
remaining, or a price per hour.

verifies.text: Rule: Capacity is shown in blocks and units, never as hours spent, reserved or remaining, or a price per hour

rules.name: Capacity types listed smallest first
rules.body: The capacity types are listed smallest first, each with a description.

verifies.text: Rule: The capacity types are listed smallest first, each with a description

rules.name: Clients never choose who works
rules.body: Clients never choose who works a block.

verifies.text: Rule: Clients never choose who works a block

rules.name: Retrying a purchase never charges twice

verifies.text: Rule: Retrying a purchase never charges twice

rules.name: A space outlasts its people
rules.why: What was said stays available with the messaging provider.
rules.body:
A space and its conversations stay when everyone has left, and when its
organization is gone.

rules.name: A team's engineers are in its clients' spaces
rules.body:
The engineers on a team, its lead included, are in the space of every client
the team is assigned to. Assigning a team to a client puts them in, and
removing it takes them out.

rules.name: Clients are invited, and some can only be emailed
rules.body:
Exalynt's people are put in a space directly. A client's people are invited
where the messaging provider requires it, and anyone it can't reach is shown as
unable to join, to be emailed instead.

rules.name: Every organization has a space
rules.body:
Every organization has a space from when it's created, and whoever creates it
is in it.

rules.name: Joining an organization puts you in its space
rules.body:
Joining an organization puts you in its space, and leaving it, or being
removed, takes you out.

rules.name: Leaving Exalynt takes you out of every space
rules.why: Someone no longer at Exalynt, or banned, must not keep reading what clients say.
rules.body:
Losing your place as one of Exalynt's people, or being banned or deleted, takes
you out of every space you're in.

rules.name: Only Exalynt sees a space from the app
rules.body:
In the app, only the engineers on a client's teams, and admins, see who is in
the client's space. The client's people see it with the messaging provider.

rules.name: Spaces follow engineers between teams
rules.body:
Joining a team puts an engineer in its clients' spaces, and leaving it takes
them out. Moving to another team does both, except for clients both teams
support.

rules.name: A block's conversations are for its client and the teams supporting it
rules.body:
The same people see a block's conversations: anyone in its organization, the
engineers on the teams assigned to it, and admins. Nobody at another client
does.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's conversations are for its client and the teams supporting it

rules.name: A subject is used once on a block
rules.body:
No two of a block's conversations with the messaging provider in use share a
subject, however it's capitalized.

verifies.text: Rule: A subject is used once on a block
