rules.name: Anyone at the client, or on a team supporting it, starts its blocks' conversations
rules.body:
Anyone in a block's organization, and the engineers on the teams assigned to
it, start conversations on its blocks. So do admins. Engineers on other teams
can't.

verifies.text: Rule: Anyone at the client, or on a team supporting it, starts its blocks' conversations

rules.name: Conversations start by hand, on a subject
rules.body:
A block has no conversations until someone starts one, on a subject they give
it. It's started in the block's organization's space, and a block can have any
number. Each stays the same conversation whoever claims or unclaims the block.

verifies.text: Rule: Conversations start by hand, on a subject

rules.name: None start on a fulfilled block
rules.body:
Once a block is fulfilled, no more conversations start on it. Those it has
stay.

verifies.text: Rule: None start on a fulfilled block

rules.name: Bios are at most 500 characters
rules.body: A bio is short, at most 500 characters.

verifies.text: Rule: A bio is short, at most 500 characters
Rule: Clearing a bio leaves none

rules.name: Who edits a bio
rules.body: An engineer edits their own bio, and Exalynt's admins can edit anyone's.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer edits their own bio, and Exalynt's admins can edit anyone's

rules.name: Who sees a bio
rules.body:
An engineer's bio is seen by their teammates and by the clients their team
supports, and by no other client.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer's bio is seen by their teammates and by the clients their team supports, and by no other client

rules.name: A Focus belongs to one estimate

verifies.text: Rule: A Focus belongs to one estimate

rules.name: Clients read only their own estimates
rules.body: A client reads their own organization's estimates and no one else's.

verifies.text: Rule: A client reads their own organization's estimates and no one else's
Rule: Deleting an estimate is permanent

rules.name: Discounts apply to the whole project
rules.body: A discount takes a percentage off the whole project.

verifies.text: Rule: A discount takes a percentage off the whole project

rules.name: Each Focus has its own pace
rules.body: Each Focus is planned at a pace, and the estimate costs every Focus at its own.

verifies.text: Rule: Each Focus is planned at a pace, and the estimate costs every Focus at its own

rules.name: Engineers work on supported clients' estimates
rules.body: An engineer works on the estimates of the clients their team supports.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer works on the estimates of the clients their team supports

rules.name: Estimates are for organizations or prospects
rules.body: An estimate is for an existing organization, or for a prospect.

verifies.text: Rule: An estimate is for an existing organization, or for a prospect

rules.name: Estimates keep their original prices
rules.body: An estimate keeps the prices it was written at.

verifies.text: Rule: An estimate keeps the prices it was written at

rules.name: Estimates record their author
rules.body: An estimate records who wrote it.

verifies.text: Rule: An estimate records who wrote it

rules.name: Focus sizes and block prices
rules.body: A Focus's size spans a range of units, and each block type prices them.

verifies.text: Rule: A Focus's size spans a range of units, and each block type prices them

rules.name: Only Exalynt writes estimates
rules.body: Only Exalynt writes, changes, and deletes estimates.

verifies.text: Rule: Only Exalynt writes, changes, and deletes estimates

rules.name: Prospects see estimates once attached
rules.body: A prospect sees their estimate only once it's attached to their organization.

verifies.text: Rule: A prospect sees their estimate only once it's attached to their organization

rules.name: Replacing replaces everything
rules.body: Replacing an estimate replaces all of it.

verifies.text: Rule: Replacing an estimate replaces all of it

rules.name: A focus is its own record
rules.body:
A focus is its own record, and can be on several of its client's blocks. A
block has at most one focus: giving it a new focus, or one of its client's
existing focuses, takes the place of the one it had, which remains. A focus
needs a title, editing it keeps it the same focus and changes it on every block
it's on, and taking it off a block keeps the focus. A block can't be given
another client's focus.

verifies.text: Rule: A focus is its own record, on any of its client's blocks

rules.name: Clients follow a block's status
rules.body:
Clients follow a block's status: in progress once it's started, then fulfilled.
A client can't mark a block fulfilled.

verifies.text: Rule: Clients follow a block's status

rules.name: Clients read a block's updates
rules.body:
Anyone who can read a block reads its updates, the client included, and another
organization can't.

verifies.text: Rule: Clients read a block's updates

rules.name: Engineers mark their blocks fulfilled
rules.body: A block's engineer marks it fulfilled. Nobody else can.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's engineer marks it fulfilled

rules.name: Engineers post updates on their blocks
rules.body:
Whoever can manage a block posts updates on it: its engineer, their lead, or an
admin, and nobody else. An update is about its block, and about the block's
focus at the time when it has one. A block with no focus still takes updates.
An update's attachments are its client's objects, never another organization's.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's engineer posts updates on it

rules.name: Engineers start their blocks from the start of the week
rules.body:
A block's engineer starts it, from the start of its week. Before then, starting
it is refused, and nobody else can start it.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's engineer starts it, from the start of its week

rules.name: Focus attachments are the client's
rules.body: A focus's attachments are its client's objects, never another organization's.

verifies.text: Rule: A focus's attachments are its client's objects

rules.name: Fulfilled is final
rules.body: Marking a block fulfilled is final.

verifies.text: Rule: Marking it fulfilled is final

rules.name: No fulfillment deadline
rules.body:
There's no deadline for fulfilling a block. A block still not fulfilled after
its week ends, started or not, can still be started and marked fulfilled later.

rules.name: Only its writer changes an update
rules.body:
Only the person who wrote an update edits or deletes it. A deleted update keeps
its place on the block, emptied, saying when it was deleted.

verifies.text: Rule: Only its writer changes an update

rules.name: Started before fulfilled
rules.body: A block must be started before it's marked fulfilled.

verifies.text: Rule: A block must be started before it's marked fulfilled

rules.name: Starting a block records who and when
rules.body: Starting a block records who started it and when.

verifies.text: Rule: Starting a block records who started it and when

rules.name: Who changes a focus
rules.body:
Only someone who can manage a block it's on, or the block's client, changes a
focus. At the client, that's a member whose role lets them change focuses,
which the Admin and Member roles do, on any of its blocks, whether or not an
engineer is on it yet. Whoever can change the focus of any of a client's blocks
can look through that client's focuses to choose one. Anyone who can read the
block, the client included, reads its focus, and another organization can't.

verifies.text: Rule: Only someone who can manage its block, or its client, changes a focus

rules.name: Clients move blocks until the week starts
rules.body: A client can move a scheduled block until its week starts.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can move a scheduled block until its week starts

rules.name: Clients of a team share room
rules.body: Clients of the same team share its room.

verifies.text: Rule: Clients of the same team share its room

rules.name: Clients unschedule blocks until the week starts
rules.body: A client can take a scheduled block out of its week until that week starts.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can take a scheduled block out of its week until that week starts

rules.name: Exalynt can move lapsed blocks
rules.body: Exalynt can move a block whose week ended with no work begun.

verifies.text: Rule: Exalynt can move a block whose week ended with no work begun

rules.name: Last in, first out, with an exact fit first
rules.why: The clients who scheduled first keep their place, and as little room as possible is given up.
rules.body:
When blocks must come out of a week to fit less room, the latest-scheduled
block whose size exactly matches the shortfall comes out first, even if later
blocks are skipped. If none matches, the latest-scheduled block comes out, and
the choice repeats until the week fits.

verifies.text: Rule: Blocks come out last in, first out, with an exact fit first

rules.name: No scheduling into a full week
rules.body: A week without room for a block can't be scheduled into.

verifies.text: Rule: A week without room for a block can't be scheduled into

rules.name: Only what can't fit comes out
rules.why: A client with several teams can be fitted by any of them, so less room on one team needn't cost it anything.
rules.body:
When blocks come out of a week to fit less room, a block whose client's teams
can still fit it stays, even if it was scheduled later.

verifies.text: Rule: Only blocks the teams can't fit come out

rules.name: Room comes from assigned teams
rules.body: A client's room comes only from the engineers on its assigned teams.

verifies.text: Rule: A client's room comes only from the engineers on its assigned teams

rules.name: Scheduling comes before work
rules.body: A block must be scheduled before it can be worked on.

verifies.text: Rule: A block must be scheduled before it can be worked on

rules.name: Starting means work has begun
rules.body: A block's engineer starting it means work on it has begun.

rules.name: The preferred week is a target
rules.body: The preferred week is a target, and a missed week doesn't cancel the block.

verifies.text: Rule: The preferred week is a target, and a missed week doesn't cancel the block

rules.name: Unscheduled blocks reserve no room
rules.body: An unscheduled block reserves no room.

verifies.text: Rule: An unscheduled block reserves no room

rules.name: Weeks are never overbooked
rules.body: A week never holds more scheduled blocks than its room fits.

rules.name: Admins resolve cross-team conflicts
rules.body: Admins can reassign blocks across teams and resolve cross-team conflicts.

rules.name: Assignment must fit availability
rules.body:
A block can't be assigned to an engineer whose effective availability that week
can't fit it alongside what they already have. Admins can't assign a block
beyond an engineer's availability for its week either.

rules.name: Assignment requires eligibility
rules.body: An engineer must be eligible when they're assigned a block.

rules.name: Claiming requires eligibility
rules.body:
An engineer must be eligible to claim a block: on a team assigned to its
client.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer must be eligible to claim a block: on a team assigned to its client

rules.name: Claiming staffs the block directly
rules.body:
Claiming puts the engineer straight on the block, with no team-held step in
between.

verifies.text: Rule: Claiming puts the engineer straight on the block, with no team-held step in between

rules.name: Claims must fit availability
rules.body:
A block can't be claimed by an engineer whose availability that week can't fit
it alongside what they already have.

verifies.text: Rule: A block can't be claimed by an engineer whose availability that week can't fit it alongside what they already have

rules.name: Engineers are never overbooked
rules.body: An engineer is never on more blocks in a week than their availability fits.

rules.name: Exalynt staff assign engineers
rules.body: Exalynt staff put an engineer on a block.

rules.name: In-progress blocks can't be moved
rules.body: Once a block is in progress, its preferred week can't be moved.

rules.name: Lapsed blocks must be moved first
rules.body:
Once its preferred week ends, an unclaimed block can't be claimed by anyone
until it's moved to an upcoming week. The client or an admin can move it, and
the client is notified when it isn't them.

verifies.text: Rule: Once its week ends, a block nobody's on can't be claimed until it's moved

rules.name: Late claims during the preferred week
rules.body:
The goal is to claim a block before its preferred week. A block still unclaimed
when the week starts can still be claimed late in that week.

verifies.text: Rule: A block nobody's on can still be claimed during its week

rules.name: Leaving a client's teams releases its upcoming blocks
rules.why: An engineer who no longer supports a client can't see or unclaim its blocks, and nobody else can claim one while they're on it.
rules.body:
An engineer who leaves a client's teams comes off its blocks whose week hasn't
started. A block whose week has started, or that work has begun on, keeps them.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer who leaves a client's teams comes off its blocks whose week hasn't started

rules.name: Listing an engineer's blocks
rules.body:
The blocks an engineer is on can be listed across every client, and narrowed to
a range of weeks.

verifies.text: Rule: The blocks an engineer is on can be listed across every client, and narrowed to a range of weeks

rules.name: New blocks start unstaffed
rules.body: A newly bought block has no engineer on it.

rules.name: No claiming an assigned block
rules.body:
An engineer can't claim a block assigned to someone else. An admin can reassign
it.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer can't claim a block someone else is on

rules.name: One engineer per block
rules.body:
A block has at most one assigned engineer and is never split across engineers.
Reassigning a block replaces its engineer and never adds a second one.

rules.name: Only capacity managers assign engineers
rules.body:
Only Exalynt staff who manage capacity put an engineer on a block. A client
can't.

rules.name: Taking an engineer off a block
rules.body:
Taking an engineer off a block clears it, and the block no longer shows among
the blocks they're on.

rules.name: Unclaiming before the week starts
rules.body:
An engineer can unclaim a block they're on until its week starts. It goes back
to nobody being on it, still in its week, for anyone eligible to claim.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer can unclaim a block they're on until its week starts

rules.name: Warned before stranding another block
rules.why: An engineer whose team supports several clients can use up the only room one client's block had, which then lapses unless an admin sorts it out.
rules.body:
An engineer is told before claiming a block that leaves another of that week's
blocks with nobody who can take it. The claim is still allowed.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer is told before claiming a block that leaves another of that week's blocks with nobody who can take it

rules.name: Fewest clients breaks ties
rules.body:
Between teams with as much unfulfilled capacity, it gets the one with the
fewest clients.

verifies.text: Rule: Between teams with as much unfulfilled capacity, it gets the one with the fewest clients

rules.name: Least unfulfilled capacity wins
rules.body: A new client gets the team with the least unfulfilled capacity.

verifies.text: Rule: A new client gets the team with the least unfulfilled capacity

rules.name: Only teams offering time qualify
rules.body: Only a team with an engineer offering time in the coming weeks can be given.

verifies.text: Rule: Only a team with an engineer offering time in the coming weeks can be given

rules.name: Signing up without a team
rules.body:
A new client signs up even when it can't be given a team, and waits for Exalynt
to assign one.

verifies.text: Rule: A new client signs up even when it can't be given a team, and waits for Exalynt to assign one

rules.name: A departing lead leaves no lead
rules.body:
When a team's lead moves to another team, their old team is left with no lead,
and they lead the new team only if put on it as lead.

verifies.text: Rule: When a team's lead moves to another team, their old team is left with no lead, and they lead the new team only if put on it as lead

rules.name: Clients can have several teams
rules.body:
A client can have several teams, and sees each by name, with its own members
and its own lead.

verifies.text: Rule: A client can have several teams, and sees each by name, with its own members and its own lead

rules.name: Clients can't see a team's other clients
rules.body:
A client sees only itself among a team's clients, never which others the team
works with.

verifies.text: Rule: A client sees only itself among a team's clients, never which others the team works with

rules.name: Clients see only their supporting teams
rules.body: A client sees only teams that support it.

verifies.text: Rule: A client sees only teams that support it

rules.name: Deleted teams disappear for clients
rules.body: Once a team is deleted, its clients no longer see it.

verifies.text: Rule: Once a team is deleted, its clients no longer see it

rules.name: Engineers work only with supported clients
rules.body:
Engineers work with a client's capacity only when their team supports that
client.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer allowed to read capacity at team scope sees only what their team supports

rules.name: Exalynt's view of teams
rules.body:
Naming a client, Exalynt sees that client's teams and every client each
supports; naming none, every team.

verifies.text: Rule: Naming a client, Exalynt sees that client's teams and every client each supports; naming none, every team

rules.name: Member access to teams follows role
rules.body: A client's members see its teams only if their role lets them.

verifies.text: Rule: A client's members see its teams only if their role lets them

rules.name: Members are listed lead first
rules.body: A team's members are listed lead first, each with their name and email address.

verifies.text: Rule: A team's members are listed lead first, each with their name and email address

rules.name: One lead per team
rules.body:
A team has at most one lead, so making someone its lead makes the old lead an
ordinary member.

verifies.text: Rule: A team has at most one lead, so making someone its lead makes the old lead an ordinary member

rules.name: One team per engineer
rules.body:
An engineer belongs to at most one team, so putting them on another moves them
off their old one.

verifies.text: Rule: An engineer belongs to at most one team, so putting them on another moves them off their old one

rules.name: Only Exalynt assigns teams
rules.body:
Only Exalynt assigns teams to clients and takes them off. A client can't give
itself a team or take one away.

verifies.text: Rule: Only Exalynt assigns teams to clients and takes them off
Rule: Only Exalynt makes teams

rules.name: Only Exalynt's people join teams
rules.body:
Only Exalynt's own people can be on a team, and someone who leaves Exalynt is
no longer shown on it.

verifies.text: Rule: Only Exalynt's own people can be on a team, and someone who leaves Exalynt is no longer shown on it

rules.name: Removed members leave every client's view
rules.body: Taking someone off a team takes them off every client's view of it.

verifies.text: Rule: Taking someone off a team takes them off every client's view of it

rules.name: Removing one team keeps the others
rules.body: Taking a client off one of its teams leaves it its other teams.

verifies.text: Rule: Taking a client off one of its teams leaves it its other teams

rules.name: Removing someone already gone
rules.body: Taking someone off a team they've already left finds nothing to take them off.

verifies.text: Rule: Taking someone off a team they've already left finds nothing to take them off

rules.name: Repeat assignment changes nothing
rules.body: Assigning a team to a client it already supports changes nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: Assigning a team to a client it already supports changes nothing

rules.name: Team names are unique
rules.body: Team names are unique, ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

verifies.text: Rule: Team names are unique, ignoring case and surrounding spaces

rules.name: Teams can support several clients
rules.body:
A team can support several clients, and Exalynt sees every client a team is
assigned to.

verifies.text: Rule: A team can support several clients, and Exalynt sees every client a team is assigned to

rules.name: What counts as a team update
rules.body: A team counts as updated when its engineers or clients change.

verifies.text: Rule: A team counts as updated when its engineers or clients change

rules.name: A partnership stands apart from organizations
rules.body:
A partnership is never a client organization, and isn't held by a person or by
a business: a solo partner manages one named after them, and an agency's
representative manages one named after the agency. Whether it pays a person or
a business is settled when its payout account is set up.

rules.name: Accepting makes the invitee manager
rules.body:
Accepting the invitation makes the invitee the partnership's manager, with the
Partner Hub.

verifies.text: Rule: Accepting the invitation makes the invitee the partnership's manager, with the Partner Hub

rules.name: Admins can adjust attribution
rules.body:
An admin can adjust attribution at any time: attribute a client, move it to
another partnership, or remove it. Typical reasons: Exalynt was already in
conversation with the client before the referral, or the client signed up
without the code. Only a partnership whose invitation has been accepted can be
attributed a client.

verifies.text: Rule: Admins can adjust attribution

rules.name: Admins set terms at invitation
rules.body:
An admin sets a partnership's terms when inviting it, and its Partner Agreement
offers them.

verifies.text: Rule: An admin sets a partnership's terms when inviting it, and its Partner Agreement offers them

rules.name: Clients see who referred them
rules.body:
A client's people see the partnership that referred it, by name, and nothing
else of it. Nobody sees who referred another client.

verifies.text: Rule: A client sees the partnership that referred it, and only its name

rules.name: Enrolling is voluntary
rules.body:
Enrolling is voluntary and never automatic, and recommending Exalynt without
being enrolled earns nothing.

rules.name: Existing accounts gain partner access
rules.body:
An invited partner who already has an account, such as an engineer or a client
member, accepts the invitation with that account and gains the Partner Hub
alongside what they already have.

rules.name: Introductions don't affect engineer assignment
rules.body:
Introducing a client doesn't assign an engineer or team to it, and nothing
prevents it either: an engineer who introduced a client can be on or lead a
team assigned to that client, and be assigned to its capacity.

rules.name: Invitations are limited
rules.body:
A partnership can send at most 50 new invitations in a day, and revoking one
doesn't free up another. Each invitation can be resent at most once a day. So
nobody is flooded with email from Exalynt.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership can send at most 50 new invitations a day
Rule: An invitation can be resent at most once a day

rules.name: Invitations can be resent or revoked
rules.body: A partner can resend or revoke an invitation until the client signs up.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner can resend or revoke an invitation until the client signs up

rules.name: Inviting creates the partnership
rules.body:
Exalynt enrolls partners by inviting them, and inviting creates the partnership
at once.

verifies.text: Rule: Exalynt enrolls partners by inviting them, and inviting creates the partnership at once

rules.name: Managers see only their own partnership
rules.body: A partnership's manager never sees or changes another partnership.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership's manager never sees or changes another partnership

rules.name: No attribution to the manager's organization
rules.body:
A partnership can't be attributed a client organization its manager is a member
of, so a manager can't use their own code.

verifies.text: Rule: A new client who signs up with a referral code is attributed to its partnership

rules.name: No earnings on other partners
rules.body:
Partners earn only on clients they introduce, never on other partners or their
introductions.

rules.name: One partnership per client
rules.body: A client has at most one partnership, and earnings are never split.

verifies.text: Rule: A client has at most one partnership

rules.name: One referral code per partnership
rules.body:
Each partnership has one referral code, shared either as the code itself or as
a sign-up link that carries it. A client who signs up with it is attributed to
that partnership automatically. Entering one is optional, and a code that
doesn't exist is refused.

verifies.text: Rule: A new client who signs up with a referral code is attributed to its partnership

rules.name: Partners invite clients by email
rules.body:
A partner can invite someone to become a client, once per address. Exalynt
sends the invitation, and it says the partner may earn from it.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner can invite someone to become a client

rules.name: Partners see each client's earning window
rules.body:
A partner sees how long their partnership earns on each of its clients: until
when, that it has no end, or that it opens with the client's first block.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner sees how long their partnership earns on each client

rules.name: Partners see only their own clients
rules.body: A partner sees the clients attributed to their partnership, and no others.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner sees the clients attributed to their partnership, and no others

rules.name: Partners see only their own invitations
rules.body:
A partner only sees and changes their own partnership's invitations, and is
never told whether an address already has an account or is already a client.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner only sees and changes their own partnership's invitations

rules.name: Partnerships can change managers
rules.body:
An admin can hand a partnership to another manager. Its referral code,
attributed clients, earnings, payouts, and payout account stay with the
partnership.

rules.name: Referral codes attribute only new clients
rules.body:
Only new clients can be attributed by referral code. Someone already at a
client can't use one to sign up again. A company with the same name as a client
isn't attributed, and nobody is told why, so a client's name never shows.

verifies.text: Rule: Referral codes attribute only new clients

rules.name: Referred clients work like any other
rules.body:
A client introduced by a partner works with Exalynt exactly as any other client
does, with the same prices and ownership.

rules.name: Revoking removes the partnership
rules.body: Revoking a partner's invitation removes the partnership it created.

verifies.text: Rule: Revoking a partner's invitation removes the partnership it created

rules.name: The code used decides the partnership
rules.body:
An invited address is attributed by the code it uses, even if another partner
invited it. With no code, it's attributed to the partner who invited it, when
just one has, and otherwise to nobody. Either way, it came by invitation when
the partnership it's attributed to invited that address, as the invitation's
link carries the code.

verifies.text: Rule: An invited address is attributed by the code it uses, or else by the one partner who invited it

rules.name: The manager names the partnership
rules.body: The manager names the partnership, and can rename it.

verifies.text: Rule: The manager names the partnership, and can rename it

rules.name: What partners can see
rules.body:
Partners see only what they need to understand their partnership and its
earnings: attributed clients' names, the capacity those clients purchased, and
what it earned. They never see a client's work or invoices.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner sees a client's name, how it came to them, and since when

rules.name: Attribution at purchase decides the partnership
rules.body:
A block earns for the partnership its client was attributed to when it bought
the block. Moving or removing the attribution later doesn't change that, and
attributing a client later doesn't reach the blocks it already bought.

verifies.text: Rule: A block earns for the partnership its client was attributed to when it bought the block

rules.name: Available teammates earn Team Support Share
rules.body: Each available teammate earns the Team Support Share of their own agreement.

verifies.text: Rule: Each available teammate earns the Team Support Share of their own agreement

rules.name: Coupons never change shares
rules.body:
Coupons and price changes change no share, and a coupon comes out of what
Exalynt keeps.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's payout basis is its capacity units × $1,750, and its price never enters it

rules.name: Each share rounds on its own
rules.body: Each share is rounded to the nearest cent on its own.

verifies.text: Rule: Each share rounds on its own

rules.name: Earning window opens at first purchase
rules.body:
A client's earning window opens at the first block it buys while attributed to
the partnership, and lasts as many months as the partnership's Earning Window
says, or has no end when its terms set no time limit. Blocks it bought before
it was attributed don't open it, and earn the partnership nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A client's earning window opens at the first block it buys while attributed to the partnership, and lasts as long as the partnership's Earning Window

rules.name: Earning windows never reset or pause
rules.body:
A client's earning window never resets or pauses. A block bought inside the
window and fulfilled after it still counts.

verifies.text: Rule: A client's earning window opens at the first block it buys while attributed to the partnership, and lasts as long as the partnership's Earning Window

rules.name: Earnings belong to the partnership
rules.body:
A partnership's earnings belong to the partnership, whoever manages it, and are
paid to its payout account, not to the individual who made the introduction.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership's earnings are its own, paid to its payout account and never its manager's

rules.name: Engineer earns the Engineer Share
rules.body:
The engineer on a block when it's fulfilled earns the Engineer Share of their
Engineer Agreement.

verifies.text: Rule: The engineer on a block when it's fulfilled earns the Engineer Share of their Engineer Agreement

rules.name: Engineering Capacity is the only basis
rules.body:
A partnership's basis says which capacity is eligible. The only basis is
Engineering Capacity (Flex, Core, or Dedicated) that referred clients purchase
within their earning window and have fulfilled.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership earns on every kind of Engineering Capacity its clients buy

rules.name: Exalynt bears partnership earnings
rules.body:
Exalynt bears partnership earnings as a separate allocation. The client's
price, the engineer share, and the team-lead share don't change.

verifies.text: Rule: Each share is worked out on its own, so no share reduces another

rules.name: Invalid payout account delays lead share
rules.body:
If the lead's payout account isn't valid when the block is fulfilled, the
team-lead share is still earned and is paid once it is.

rules.name: Manager controls the partnership's payout account
rules.body:
Only a partnership's manager can set up or change its payout account, which is
the partnership's own, separate from any the manager has as an engineer.

verifies.text: Rule: Only a partnership's manager sets up, sees or changes its payout account

rules.name: No lead means no lead share
rules.body:
If the team has no lead when the block is Fulfilled, no team-lead share is
earned. A lead appointed later doesn't get it retroactively.

rules.name: One team-lead share per block
rules.body:
A block creates at most one team-lead share, even when several teams serve the
client.

rules.name: Partner status leaves engineers unchanged
rules.body: Being a partner doesn't change an engineer's share, team, or lead status.

rules.name: Partners see only their partnership's earnings
rules.body:
A partnership's manager sees its earnings, each with its client, block, payout
basis, percentage, and amount, and never another partnership's. They aren't
told who worked a block.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner sees only their own partnership's earnings

rules.name: Partnership share earned at fulfillment
rules.body: A partnership's share is earned when the block is fulfilled, and not before.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership earns the Referral Share of its Partner Agreement on its client's blocks, once each is fulfilled

rules.name: Partnership share of payout basis
rules.body:
A partnership's share is a percentage of the capacity payout basis of eligible
capacity. It isn't a share of the price, the invoice, or the engineer share,
and it excludes the operations fee, infrastructure pass-through, taxes, and
anything that isn't Engineering Capacity.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership earns the Referral Share of its Partner Agreement on its client's blocks, once each is fulfilled

rules.name: Partnership terms set at invitation
rules.body:
A partnership earns on the terms Exalynt set when inviting it: its share, its
basis, and its earning window. The default is 5% of the engineering capacity
referred clients purchase and have fulfilled within 12 months.

verifies.text: Rule: An admin sets a partnership's terms when inviting it, and its Partner Agreement offers them

rules.name: Partnerships earn under their agreement in effect
rules.body:
A partnership earns the Referral Share of its Partner Agreement in effect when
the block is fulfilled. With none in effect then, it earns nothing on that
block.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership earns the Referral Share of its Partner Agreement on its client's blocks, once each is fulfilled

rules.name: Partnerships earn without a payout account
rules.body:
A partnership earns on its eligible blocks whether or not it has a payout
account. Like engineer and team-lead shares, its share is held until it has a
payout account that can receive it, then paid.

verifies.text: Rule: Earnings wait while their payee has no valid account, then go in the first payout after it's valid

rules.name: Payout basis per capacity unit
rules.body:
A block's payout basis is its capacity units × $1,750, and its price never
enters it.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's payout basis is its capacity units × $1,750, and its price never enters it

rules.name: Reassignment before fulfillment earns nothing
rules.body:
A block reassigned before it's fulfilled earns its earlier engineer nothing
here. Anything owed for partial work is settled under their agreement.

rules.name: Refunds after fulfillment change nothing
rules.body:
A refund or failed payment after a block is fulfilled doesn't change a share.
Exalynt absorbs it.

rules.name: Shares don't reduce each other
rules.body: Each share is worked out on its own, so no share reduces another.

verifies.text: Rule: Each share is worked out on its own, so no share reduces another

rules.name: Shares earned at fulfillment
rules.body: A block's shares are earned when it's fulfilled, and not before.

verifies.text: Rule: A block's shares are earned when it's fulfilled, and not before

rules.name: Team leads earn Team Lead Share
rules.body:
The engineer's team lead earns the Team Lead Share of their own agreement, but
not on their own block.

verifies.text: Rule: The engineer's team lead earns the Team Lead Share of their own agreement, but not on their own block

rules.name: Unclaimed shares stay with Exalynt
rules.body:
A share that doesn't apply goes to nobody else. With no lead, no available
teammates, or no partnership, Exalynt keeps it.

verifies.text: Rule: Each share is worked out on its own, so no share reduces another

rules.name: Unfulfilled capacity earns partnerships nothing
rules.body: Capacity that's never fulfilled earns a partnership nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership earns the Referral Share of its Partner Agreement on its client's blocks, once each is fulfilled

rules.name: Unlisted shares earn nothing
rules.body:
A share someone's agreement in effect doesn't list, or having none in effect,
earns them nothing.

verifies.text: Rule: A share someone's agreement in effect doesn't list, or having none in effect, earns them nothing

rules.name: When basis and percentages are fixed
rules.body:
A block's basis is fixed when it's bought, and its percentages when it's
assigned. A later basis change applies only to blocks bought after it, and
reassigning a block fixes its percentages again for its new engineer.

rules.name: When team support earners are fixed
rules.body:
Which teammates earn team support is fixed when the block is Fulfilled: those
on a team with its owning engineer at that moment, other than that team's lead,
with some availability in the block's week. A team change after that doesn't
alter it.

rules.name: When the team-lead beneficiary is fixed
rules.body:
The team-lead share's beneficiary is fixed when the block is Fulfilled: whoever
holds the role of team lead, at that moment, of a team the owning engineer is
on. A change of lead or team after that doesn't change it.

rules.name: A partnership's payout account is its own
rules.why: Partnerships are separate payees, whether a person or a business stands behind them, and keep their account when they change managers.
rules.body:
A partnership has its own payout account, apart from its manager's and from any
other partnership's, so someone managing several sets each one up.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership's payout account is its own

rules.name: Admins see only payment readiness
rules.body:
An admin sees whether an engineer can be paid, and nothing else about their
account.

verifies.text: Rule: An admin sees whether an engineer can be paid, and nothing else about their account

rules.name: Limited tokens can't reach payout accounts
rules.body: A limited token can't reach its creator's payout account.

verifies.text: Rule: A limited token can't reach its creator's payout account

rules.name: One payout account per person
rules.body: A person has at most one payout account, and a new one replaces it.

verifies.text: Rule: A person has at most one payout account, and a new one replaces it

rules.name: Payout accounts stay private to their owner
rules.body: People see and change only their own payout account.

verifies.text: Rule: People see and change only their own payout account

rules.name: Removing a payout account
rules.why: The payments partner holds a payout until it reaches the bank, and won't close an account while it does.
rules.body:
A person, or a partnership's manager, can remove its payout account, except
while money paid to it is still on its way to the bank.

verifies.text: Rule: A payout account can be removed, except while a payout is on its way to it

rules.name: Seeing whether an account can be paid
rules.body: A person sees whether their account can be paid, and what to fix if not.

verifies.text: Rule: A person sees whether their account can be paid, and what to fix if not

rules.name: Admins release payouts
rules.body: An admin sees and releases payouts, and nothing is sent without that.

verifies.text: Rule: An admin sees and releases each run, and nothing is sent without that

rules.name: Canceled payouts leave earnings unsent
rules.body:
A payout canceled before any money leaves is Canceled, and its earnings stay
unsent.

verifies.text: Rule: A payout canceled before any money leaves is Canceled, and its earnings stay unsent

rules.name: Each earning shows where it stands
rules.body: Each earning shows where it stands, and earnings on hold say what to fix.

verifies.text: Rule: Each earning shows where it stands, and earnings on hold say what to fix

rules.name: Earnings are paid after leaving
rules.body: Earnings are still paid after someone leaves their team or Exalynt.

verifies.text: Rule: Earnings are still paid after someone leaves

rules.name: Earnings are paid out when approved
rules.body:
Earnings are paid out when approved by an admin, usually once per week. A
release covers all unsent earnings from blocks fulfilled by the end of the
previous Sunday, UTC, so a week nobody released goes in the next one. Every
earning is paid eventually.

verifies.text: Rule: Exalynt aims for weekly payouts, each covering all unsent earnings fulfilled by the end of the previous Sunday, UTC

rules.name: Earnings are sent only once
rules.body: Earnings are only ever sent once.

verifies.text: Rule: Earnings are only ever sent once

rules.name: Earnings show payout outcome
rules.body:
Once payouts are sent, each earning also shows that it's waiting to be
released, processing, paid, or failed.

verifies.text: Rule: Earnings show whether they're waiting, processing, paid, or failed

rules.name: Earnings wait for a valid account
rules.body:
Earnings wait while their payee has no valid account, then go in the first
payout after it's valid.

verifies.text: Rule: Earnings wait while their payee has no valid account, then go in the first payout after it's valid

rules.name: Expected pay visible from assignment
rules.body: From assignment, people can see what a block will pay them.

verifies.text: Rule: From assignment, people can see what a block will pay them

rules.name: Failed payouts are sent again
rules.body:
A failed payout's earnings go out in a new payout once there's an account that
can receive them. The failed one says why and links to the new one.

verifies.text: Rule: A failed payout's earnings go out in a new payout, and the failed one says why and links to it

rules.name: How a payout's status progresses
rules.body:
A payout is Processing once sent, then Paid when the payment provider posts it,
or Failed if it's returned. A Paid payout becomes Failed only if the payment
provider returns it later. The one in use posts a payout as soon as it's sent,
pays it on to the bank itself, and keeps for the payee anything the bank sends
back, so its payouts stay Paid.

verifies.text: Rule: A payout is Processing once sent, Paid when the payment provider posts it, and Failed if it's returned

rules.name: No minimum payout
rules.body: There's no minimum payout.

verifies.text: Rule: There's no minimum payout

rules.name: One payout per payee per run
rules.body:
A payee gets one payout per payout run, which can cover any number of earnings
of any kind. Each line shows its block, client, basis, percentage, and amount.

verifies.text: Rule: A payee gets one payout per run, covering any number of earnings

rules.name: Partners see only their partnership's payouts
rules.body:
A partnership's manager sees only the payouts sent to that partnership, with
the bank account each went to. An admin sees them too, without the account.

verifies.text: Rule: A partner sees only their own partnership's payouts, and an admin sees them without the account

rules.name: Partnership earnings are paid separately
rules.body:
A partnership's earnings go in their own payout to its account, even when its
manager is also an engineer.

verifies.text: Rule: A partnership's earnings are its own, paid to its payout account and never its manager's

rules.name: Payouts are in US dollars
rules.body:
Earnings are earned and sent in US dollars. Exalynt pays the sending fee, and
the payee bears any currency conversion.

verifies.text: Rule: Payouts are sent in US dollars

rules.name: Payouts go to the current account
rules.body:
A payout goes to the payee's payout account when it's sent. Changing the
account affects later payouts only.

verifies.text: Rule: A payout goes to the payee's account when it's sent

rules.name: People see only their own earnings

verifies.text: Rule: People see only their own earnings

rules.name: Sent payouts aren't taken back
rules.body:
A sent payout isn't taken back here. Corrections are settled outside the
product.

rules.name: Sent payouts never change
rules.body:
What a sent payout lists never changes, whatever later happens to the basis,
earnings, or teams.

verifies.text: Rule: What a sent payout lists never changes

rules.name: Who sees payout status
rules.body:
A lead sees the payout status of their team's blocks, not what anyone else
earns. An admin sees everyone's.

verifies.text: Rule: People see their own payouts, and an admin sees everyone's

concepts.name: Access token
concepts.description: A personal access token lets someone's scripts and tools call the API as them.

confusedWith.summary: a role says what someone may do. A token only identifies who is calling.

concepts.body:
A token is a person's own, not an [organization](organization.md)'s, and holds no
access of its own: it acts with its user's [roles](role.md), so a change to those
applies at once. It has a name, an optional description, and an optional expiry.

A limited token is one limited, when it's created, to some of the organizations
its user belongs to, so it works only in those. Any other works in all of them.

concepts.name: Organization
concepts.description: An organization is a client of Exalynt: the account its people share, which buys capacity and is billed.

confusedWith.summary: an organization's members are its own people. A team is Exalynt's people, assigned to work with it.
a partnership is its own record, separate from any client organization.

concepts.body:
It holds members, each with one organization [role](role.md), and pending
invitations for people who haven't joined yet. A person can belong to several
organizations, with a role in each. Engineering [teams](../../capacity/concepts/team.md) are assigned to
it, and a client can have any number of them. Its billing details are held by
the payment provider.

concepts.name: Role
concepts.description: A role is a named set of permissions that says what someone may do. There are two kinds: platform roles, for people who work with Exalynt, and organization roles, for a client [organization](organization.md)'s members.

confusedWith.summary: a token holds no access of its own. It acts with its user's roles.

concepts.body:
A permission is something checked before it's done, such as scheduling a block.
It says what may be done, never where.

A platform role says what someone who works with Exalynt may do when they aren't
acting in any organization. It grants each permission at a scope, how far that
permission reaches from the person holding it: their own, their
[team](../../capacity/concepts/team.md)'s, or everything. A person holds at most one platform role.

An organization role says what a member of an organization may do in that
organization, each permission reaching that organization and no further. A
member holds exactly one in each organization they belong to, such as Admin,
Member, or Billing. Organization roles are shared by every organization, not made
per organization, and one of them is the role given to whoever creates an
organization.

One role applies at a time, by where someone is acting. The two kinds never
merge.

Which of Exalynt's applications someone is offered belongs to them directly, not
to a role.

concepts.name: Agreement
concepts.description: The terms a party has with Exalynt. There are three types: a Client Agreement for an [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md), an Engineer Agreement for someone who works in the console, which covers leading a team too, and a Partner Agreement for a [partnership](../../partnerships/concepts/partnership.md).

confusedWith.summary: the partner's own record. Its terms are held in its Partner Agreement.

concepts.body:
- **Agreement Template**: a type of agreement's text.
- **Agreement Version**: one version of a template.
- **Standard Terms**: what every party of a type shares.
- **Commercial Terms**: what's agreed with the named party, as a list of terms
  chosen from a catalog, such as an Engineer Share or a Referral Share. Each term
  applies only if it's listed.
- **Accepted Agreement**: the exact text and Commercial Terms someone accepted,
  kept as accepted.

A shared list of definitions gives the meaning of the words every agreement uses.
A [payout share](../../pay/concepts/payout-share.md) comes from the Commercial Terms of the agreement
in effect.

## Lifecycle

1. Offered
2. Accepted
3. In effect
4. Superseded

An agreement is offered to a party, who accepts it. The latest accepted is in
effect, until a later one is accepted and supersedes it.

concepts.name: Invoice
concepts.description: What a purchase of capacity issues. Exalynt keeps a small record of it that links it to the payment provider and to the [blocks](../../capacity/concepts/capacity-block.md) it bought; the provider holds everything else about it, including the tax it worked out and added to it.
concepts.body:
Each block bought on an invoice points at it. An invoice's status is separate from
the status of any payment on it: one whose payment is clearing or has failed still
reads Open, and that payment shows on its blocks. Each payment provider's own
statuses map onto Exalynt's.

## Lifecycle

1. Draft
2. Open
3. Paid, Void, or Uncollectible

An invoice stays open if a payment on it didn't go through, or is still
clearing. Paying it makes it Paid. Voiding it makes it Void, and Uncollectible
means it's been written off.

concepts.name: Capacity block
concepts.description: One purchase of Engineering Capacity, scheduled into a single week. Its type sets its size: **Flex** is 1 [unit](capacity-unit.md), **Core** 2, and **Dedicated** 4.

confusedWith.summary: a quarter of one engineer's week, the size a block is measured in.
a separate lifecycle that starts once a block is fulfilled. A fulfilled block isn't necessarily paid out.

concepts.body:
A block belongs to the [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) that bought it, and is
numbered in turn within it, keeping its number, such as BLK-0001. Once
scheduled, it has a [preferred week](preferred-week.md), and it sits in the
client's [shared queue](shared-queue.md) until it has an engineer. It can have a
[focus](focus.md) saying what its work is about.

## Lifecycle

1. Pending payment (while the client's payment clears)
2. Unscheduled
3. Scheduled, unassigned (in the client's shared queue)
4. Assigned
5. In progress (once its engineer starts it, from the start of its week)
6. Fulfilled (once its engineer marks it fulfilled)

Purchasing, scheduling, assignment, starting, and fulfilling are separate steps.
Nobody reviews a block: it's [fulfilled](fulfilled.md) once its engineer marks
it so.

concepts.name: Capacity unit
concepts.description: A quarter of one engineer's week. Clients see units and blocks, never hours.

confusedWith.summary: one purchase, which holds one or more units.

concepts.body:
A [capacity block](capacity-block.md) holds 1, 2, or 4 units, depending on its
type. An engineer's [effective availability](effective-availability.md) for a
week is measured in units, from 0 to 4.

concepts.name: Conversation
concepts.description: A conversation is the talk about one subject on a [capacity block](capacity-block.md), in its organization's [space](space.md). A block has any number, each on a subject of its own.
concepts.body:
Someone starts a conversation by giving it a subject, such as "Rate file
format". With the messaging provider it opens with the block's number before
the subject, "BLK-0037 - Rate file format", since the space holds every
block's conversations. Everyone in the space can read and join it; it has no
people of its own.

What's said stays with the messaging provider. The app reads only how many
messages a conversation has, when the latest was sent, and how many one of
Exalynt's people hasn't read, which the messaging provider can't say for a
client's.

## Lifecycle

1. Started

A conversation is recorded once the messaging provider has started it, and stays
for good.

concepts.name: Effective availability
concepts.description: An engineer's weekly baseline plus their one-off adjustments.
concepts.body:
It's how much of a given week the engineer offers, in
[capacity units](capacity-unit.md), from 0 to 4. The baseline is what they offer
every week. An adjustment replaces it for the weeks it covers, and a week with
neither offers nothing.

concepts.name: Eligible engineer
concepts.description: An engineer on a team assigned to the purchasing client.
concepts.body:
Eligibility is about a [capacity block](capacity-block.md)'s client: an engineer
is eligible for the blocks of the client [organizations](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) their
[team](team.md) is assigned to.

concepts.name: Estimate
concepts.description: Exalynt's planning aid for what a project might take. It is not a quote.

confusedWith.summary: what one block's work is about. An estimate's focuses only group and size planned work.

concepts.body:
An estimate is an ordered list of focuses, each sized S, M, L, or XL
and planned at a pace, with an optional description and ordered notes. A focus is
whatever the work is grouped by: a new feature, or an improvement or enhancement
to an existing system.

Sizes span ranges of [capacity units](capacity-unit.md), which add up to the
estimate's totals. A focus's pace is the [block](capacity-block.md) type (Flex,
Core, or Dedicated) bought and used once a week for it, which sets its price per
unit and how many weeks its size takes. A focus written without one is planned at
Dedicated. Every focus, and the project, is still shown on every block, so the
client sees what each would cost and take.

An estimate can also carry discounts, each a whole-number percentage off the
whole project. It belongs to an [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md), or to none, such
as a prospect's before they sign up.

concepts.name: Focus
concepts.description: What a [capacity block](capacity-block.md)'s work is about: a title, an optional description, and the images, videos, and files that go with it.

confusedWith.summary: an estimate's focuses are how planned work is grouped and sized. A block's focus says what one block's work is about, and isn't taken from an estimate.

concepts.body:
A focus belongs to the [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) whose blocks it's on, and
its images, videos, and files are that organization's uploaded files. Each image
or video can have a caption. It's its own record and can be on several of its
organization's blocks, such as work that runs over several weeks, while a block
has at most one focus. Taken off its blocks, a focus remains.

concepts.name: Fulfilled
concepts.description: A block is fulfilled once its engineer marks it fulfilled. Nobody reviews it, and marking it fulfilled is final.

confusedWith.summary: a separate lifecycle that starts once a block is fulfilled. A fulfilled block isn't necessarily paid out.

concepts.body:
Fulfilled describes a [capacity block](capacity-block.md) that has reached
Fulfilled in its lifecycle. It keeps when it was fulfilled. A block fulfilled
before review was removed keeps its approval's time.

concepts.name: Preferred week
concepts.description: The week a client schedules a block for. It's a target Exalynt strives for, not a guarantee.
concepts.body: Each scheduled [capacity block](capacity-block.md) has one preferred week.

concepts.name: Shared queue
concepts.description: Each client's scheduled, unassigned blocks. Engineers and leads on any team assigned to that client can see it, and no team owns it.
concepts.body:
Each client [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) has one shared queue, made up of its
[capacity blocks](capacity-block.md) that have a
[preferred week](preferred-week.md) and no engineer yet. The
[teams](team.md) assigned to the client see the same queue.

concepts.name: Space membership
concepts.description: A space membership is someone's place in a [space](space.md): that they're in it, or invited, or that the messaging provider can't reach them.

confusedWith.summary: membership: being one of an organization's people is what puts someone in its space, not the same thing.

concepts.body:
Each membership is one person in one space. Exalynt's people are put in
directly. A client's people may be invited instead, where the messaging provider
requires it, and are in once they accept. Someone the messaging provider can't
reach, such as a client with no account there, can't join and is emailed
instead.

## Lifecycle

1. Invited
2. Member

Accepting the messaging provider's invitation makes someone a member. Someone
who can't join stays unable to until they're added again. Being taken out of the
space ends a membership at any point.

concepts.name: Space
concepts.description: A space is where people talk about the work with the messaging provider, outside the app or inside it. Every [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) has one, its conversation space.

confusedWith.summary: a team is a group of Exalynt's people. A space holds a team's engineers and a client's people together.

concepts.body:
A space has a name, which is its organization's when it's made, and the people
put in it, each with a [space membership](space-membership.md). It holds the
[conversations](conversation.md) about its organization's blocks.

A space stands on its own: an organization points at its space, but the space
doesn't belong to anything, so it outlasts everyone in it. Its people are the
organization's own and the engineers on the [teams](team.md) assigned to it, so
it's the one place a client and Exalynt's people share.

What's said in a space stays with the messaging provider. The app keeps only
which space is which, and who it put there.

concepts.name: Team
concepts.description: A team is a group of Exalynt's people who work with the clients it's assigned to. It decides who at Exalynt a client sees.

confusedWith.summary: a client's members are that organization's own people. A team's members are Exalynt's people.

concepts.body:
A team has a name, a set of members, at most one of them its lead, and the
[organizations](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md) it's assigned to as clients. A team can support
any number of clients, and a client can have any number of teams. A person is on
at most one team.

A team lead is an engineer an admin designates as a team's lead, with everything
an engineer can do too.

concepts.name: Partnership
concepts.description: A partner's own record in the Partnership Program, separate from any client [organization](../../accounts/concepts/organization.md): a solo partner's is named after them, and an agency's after the agency, managed by its representative.

confusedWith.summary: a client company's account. A partnership is never one.

concepts.body:
A partnership has one manager, a person, who can manage several. It has the name
its manager gives it, a referral code, the clients attributed to it, and terms:
its share, what it's a share of, and how long it earns on each client, or no time
limit.

Its share is a [payout share](../../pay/concepts/payout-share.md) of the
[capacity payout basis](../../pay/concepts/capacity-payout-basis.md) of the engineering capacity its
attributed clients purchase and have fulfilled. How long it earns on each client
is its earning window.

Whether it pays a person or a business is settled when its payout account is set
up. Its terms are set out in its Partner [Agreement](../../agreements/concepts/agreement.md).

concepts.name: Capacity payout basis
concepts.description: The amount that engineer, team-lead, and partnership shares of a block are calculated from.

confusedWith.summary: what a client buys, at a price the basis doesn't depend on.
one person's or partnership's part of the basis, not the basis itself.

concepts.body:
A [capacity block](../../capacity/concepts/capacity-block.md)'s basis comes from its
[capacity units](../../capacity/concepts/capacity-unit.md), not from the price the client paid. Each
[payout share](payout-share.md), team support included, is a percentage of it.

concepts.name: Payout share
concepts.description: One part of a [capacity block](../../capacity/concepts/capacity-block.md)'s [capacity payout basis](capacity-payout-basis.md), owed to whoever earned it. Also called an earning.

confusedWith.summary: money sent, made up of earnings. A share is what's owed, and it exists before any payout does.
the whole amount a share is a percentage of.

concepts.body:
A block can have these shares:

- **Engineer share**: for the engineer on the block.
- **Team support share**: for each teammate with availability in the block's
  week.
- **Team-lead share**: for the lead of that engineer's team.
- **Partnership share**: for the [partnership](../../partnerships/concepts/partnership.md) that introduced
  the client.

Each share is a percentage of the basis. An earning has a kind, and more kinds
of paid work may come. A [payout](payout.md) is made up of earnings.

## Lifecycle

1. Upcoming
2. Earned
3. Sent
4. Paid

A share is upcoming from when the block is assigned, and earned when the block
is fulfilled. An earned share can be on hold while its payee has no payout
account that can be paid. It's sent when a payout carries it, and paid once that
payout has arrived.

concepts.name: Payout
concepts.description: Money sent to a payee, made up of earnings. A payout is always current or historical, never in the future: what's still to come is earnings.

confusedWith.summary: what someone is owed from a block, which exists from when the block is assigned. A payout is the money that pays it.

concepts.body:
A payout is made up of earnings, which come from [payout shares](payout-share.md)
among other things, and has no kind of its own. It goes to the payee's payout
account, which is one bank account.

## Lifecycle

1. Processing
2. Paid, or Failed, or Canceled. A Paid payout can still become Failed if the
   bank returns it.

A separate lifecycle that starts once a block is fulfilled. Each of its payout
shares (engineer, team support, team lead, partnership) moves through its own
payout and payment statuses. A fulfilled block isn't necessarily paid out.

personas.name: Theo Lindqvist
personas.title: Founder
personas.description: Founder of an early-stage startup with no full engineering team, buying engineering to build the product.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To buy engineering capacity and book it into a week straight away, so work
  starts without the wait of hiring.
- To see what's still needed before work can start, and what happens next.
- To know what each piece of the product will cost and how many weeks it takes,
  from Exalynt's estimates, so they can plan within tight money.
- To see every week who's on each block, what it's about, and when it's
  fulfilled, so they can tell what the money bought.

## Knows

Their market and what the product should do. Semi-technical: reads some code and
may have sketched a prototype with AI. New to Exalynt's terms.

## Context

Laptop and phone, once or twice a week around checkpoints, fitted between
customer and investor conversations. Money is tight and things feel urgent.

## Expects

To talk in MVPs and roadmaps, iterate quickly, and compare Exalynt with hiring a
contractor.

## Cares about

Visible progress every week for the money spent. Gives up if they can't tell
what they paid for or what happens next, or if starting work feels slow.

personas.name: Helen Marsh
personas.title: Director of operations
personas.description: Director of operations at a mid-sized equipment-rental business. Buys and steers custom software from Exalynt, and owns the budget and the relationship.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To buy blocks and schedule them for the weeks that suit the business, in a few
  minutes between meetings.
- To see where the work stands each week, and the named engineer on each block,
  without having to ask.
- To know what the work will cost and how many weeks it takes, from Exalynt's
  estimates, so they can plan the budget.
- To bring colleagues in and give each the right role, so others can follow the
  work or pay the invoices.

## Knows

Their business and its processes in depth. Doesn't code. Has worked with
software vendors, but blocks of capacity are new.

## Context

Laptop, between meetings, once or twice a week around checkpoints. Buys and
schedules in short, interrupted sittings.

## Expects

To talk in weeks, budget and outcomes, never hours. "Sprint" and "ticket" mean
little. Expects plain language and ordinary vendor invoices.

## Cares about

Seeing real progress and a named engineer. Gives up if they can't tell what they
paid for or what happens next.

personas.name: Owen Achebe
personas.title: Controller
personas.description: Controller at a client business who pays invoices and manages payment methods and billing details.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To keep the company's payment methods current, and choose the one charged by
  default.
- To find every invoice, with its tax and payment status, and download it to
  file.
- To be told at once when a payment fails, and pay the unpaid invoice, so the
  blocks it bought aren't left waiting.

## Knows

Accounts payable and the company's cards. Little about the engineering: a block
is a line item.

## Context

Laptop, a few times a month in batches, or when a failed-payment notice arrives.
Pressed at month end.

## Expects

An invoice list, statuses and a downloadable PDF, like any vendor portal.

## Cares about

Amounts that match and are easy to file. Gives up if invoices are hard to find
or a failed payment is unclear.

personas.name: Carla Nuñez
personas.title: Customer service manager
personas.description: Customer service manager at a non-software business whose team uses what Exalynt builds. Follows the work and raises what the software should do.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To see where each block stands, and read its focus and updates, without having
  to ask for them.
- To say what a block should work on, in their own words and with their own
  screenshots and files, so what they asked for reaches the engineers.
- To talk with the engineers about a block, and know they were heard.
- To move a block to another week before it starts, when the business needs it.

## Knows

The daily process and its exceptions. Not technical. Didn't choose Exalynt, and
can't buy capacity or see billing.

## Context

Laptop, between calls, once or twice a week. Mostly reads where the work stands,
and sometimes moves a block.

## Expects

To talk about customers and cases, and to find updates without having to ask for
them.

## Cares about

Whether what they asked for moved. Gives up if updates read as technical, or if
it's unclear anyone heard them.

personas.name: Mira Castellan
personas.title: Founder-operator
personas.description: Founder-operator who runs Exalynt's staffing, payouts, estimates, partnerships and roles, while also talking to clients and doing engineering.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To spot what needs them at once: scheduled blocks nobody's on, overbooked
  weeks, failed payments, and earnings on hold, and be told when one comes up.
- To put an eligible engineer on a block, or take one off, across every client
  and team.
- To see the week's payouts by payee, with what each line is for, before
  releasing them, so money moves only once it's been checked.
- To bring engineers and partners in on the terms chosen, and see when each
  engineer is ready for client work.

## Knows

Every rule, and is technical. Will use the API where the UI has no way to do
something.

## Context

Desktop, daily, in short bursts between calls and engineering. Approves and
releases payouts, usually once per week.

## Expects

Exalynt's own vocabulary, views that lead with exceptions, and notifications
that say when something needs them.

## Cares about

Spotting unassigned blocks, failed payments and shares on hold right away. Gives
up on anything that hides exceptions, makes money moves hard to double-check, or
needs a long unbroken sitting.

personas.name: Lena Fischer
personas.title: Senior full-stack engineer
personas.description: Senior full-stack engineer, long at Exalynt, on a team assigned to a few clients. Owns blocks end to end, from starting one to marking it fulfilled.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To set their availability once, and change a week when they need to, so
  clients schedule only what they can do.
- To claim the blocks that fit their weeks, seeing what each will earn them
  before they claim it.
- To start a block, post what they did, and mark it fulfilled in a few clicks,
  so the app stays out of the way of the work.
- To see what each block earned and when it was paid, with numbers that match.

## Knows

Blocks and the client's business. Skips instructions and moves fast.

## Context

Laptop, at the start and end of the week around blocks. Coding is the real job.

## Expects

GitHub and Linear-style speed, with the app staying out of the way.

## Cares about

Knowing what a block pays before starting, and numbers that match. Gives up on
anything that makes saying what they did feel like a timesheet.

personas.name: Ravi Menon
personas.title: Associate engineer
personas.description: Recently joined Associate engineer on Lena's team, learning to own blocks end to end.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To know what's expected of them in a block's week, and what it will earn them,
  before they claim it.
- To be told why a block doesn't fit them, or why their earnings are on hold and
  what to fix, rather than just being refused.
- To see where each of their blocks stands and what its next step is, so they
  don't get it wrong in front of a client.
- To set up the bank account their payouts go to, and see whether it can be
  paid.

## Knows

Solid coding, less client experience. Unsure of terms like eligibility, shares
and Planned, and may still be setting up their payout account.

## Context

Laptop, at the start and end of the week around blocks. Reads carefully and goes
slower.

## Expects

Tools like GitHub and Linear, plus an explanation when Exalynt's process differs
from them.

## Cares about

Not doing it wrong in front of a client, knowing what a block pays, and why they
can't be assigned if that happens. Gives up on unexplained refusals and terms.

personas.name: Theo Lindqvist
personas.title: Full-stack engineer
personas.description: Mid-level full-stack engineer just hired by Exalynt, coming from a product company or agency. Will work blocks for the clients their team supports, and is paid per block rather than a salary.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To read the terms that set what they earn, and accept their Engineer
  Agreement, so they know how and when they'll be paid.
- To see what they have left to set up, and whether they're ready for client
  work, so nothing is missed before a client depends on them.
- To add their bank account on the payments partner's form, knowing Exalynt's
  admins never see its details.
- Once ready, to be told where to find their first block.

## Knows

Strong technically. Knows from their hiring conversation that Exalynt sells
blocks of engineering capacity and pays per block. Has never seen the app, and
doesn't know terms like preferred week, baseline or team support.

## Context

Laptop, one sitting after their current work, opening the email within a day.

## Expects

Setup like GitHub or Linear, a clear list of what's left, and someone to ask if
stuck, without wanting to bother the person who hired them.

## Cares about

Knowing they've done everything needed before a client depends on them, and when
and how they'll get paid. Hesitant to hand over bank details without knowing why
or who holds them. Gives up on dead ends and on not being able to tell if
anything is left to do.

mechanisms.name: API docs
mechanisms.description: The reference at `GET /docs/api`: the OpenAPI spec bundled into one document, rendered by Scalar, with each endpoint's stability and each group's maturity drawn on top by our own script.
mechanisms.body:
- `NewDocsHandler` bundles the spec once at startup, inlining every `$ref`.
  An operation without a valid `x-stability` fails the bundle, so the API
  won't start rather than serve an unlabeled endpoint.
- The bundler gives each operation below GA an `x-badges` badge, ending its
  name with an invisible U+2060 so the script can find exactly those badges.
  It also writes every operation's level, each tag's levels, and the tags'
  navigation order into `window.EXALYNT_STABILITY` on the page. The script
  needs that because Scalar only draws a tag's operations once it's opened.
- `stability-marks.js` watches Scalar's DOM and, as it renders, swaps those
  badges for stability marks, adds a mark to each operation and a maturity
  ring to each tag in the navigation, and adds the overview under the
  introduction's `## Maturity` heading. Renaming that heading in `api.yaml`
  changes the id the script looks for, and the overview silently disappears.
- The levels, their colors and wording, and how maturity is weighted mirror
  the design package's `stability/stability.ts` and `maturity/maturity.ts`.
  They change there first, then here.
- Scalar's markdown styles start with `.scalar-app .markdown`, and are loaded
  after ours, so styles for anything we add inside the introduction start the
  same way, or Scalar's list and link styles win.
- The script relies on `li[data-sidebar-id]` links to `#tag/<slug>` in the
  navigation, the `group/button-label` class, and each introduction heading
  in its own child of `.introduction-description` with an id ending
  `/description/<slug>`. That was checked by hand against Scalar on
  2026-11-16. When Scalar changes them, the page falls back to Scalar's plain
  badges and the overview's explanation alone.

mechanisms.name: Authentication
mechanisms.description: Decides who is calling each request, and puts the `authz.Principal` the rest of the API works from on the context. Clerk only signs people in: users are copied to our database, and organizations, memberships, and roles are the API's own.
mechanisms.body:
```text
Authorization: Bearer <Clerk session JWT, or exa_pat_ token>
X-Organization-ID: <our organization ID>          (optional)
        │
        ▼
authn   TokenVerifier          signature, issuer, expiry, azp → Claims
        │                      (exa_pat_ skips this: AccessTokenResolver finds the user)
        ▼
authn   Resolver               finds the user; with the header, checks membership and
        │                      loads their organization role, without it, their platform role
        ▼
authz   New…Principal          each permission → Bounds → Principal on the context
```

One role applies per request, and the two kinds never merge. With
`X-Organization-ID` it's the caller's role in that organization, once our
database confirms they're a member, or the request is a `403`. Without it, it's
their platform role, if they have one. What a role then allows is in the
[authorization doc](authorization.md).

**Personal access tokens** only identify the user who created one. The token is
found by the SHA-256 of its secret, and from the user on the request resolves
through `Resolver.ResolveUser`, exactly as a session's would. A token holds no
grants of its own, so a change to its user's roles or memberships applies to its
next request. `Principal.AccessTokenID` says a token authenticated the request.

**Service actors** aren't users. The Clerk and Stripe webhooks, identity sync,
and `api sync` each act as `authz.ServicePrincipal(id)`, with a fixed user ID
from `internal/authn/webhookusers.go` and `authz.All` for every permission.

**A user Clerk knows and we don't yet.** Our users normally follow Clerk by
webhook. Every session route uses `authn.SyncingResolver`, which, when the
caller's user isn't found, fetches them from Clerk as the identity-sync service
actor and resolves once more. It only runs with `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` set, and
only because the user is missing, never because someone isn't a member or a
record is out of bounds.

**A Principal can't be forged.** Only `authz.ContextWithPrincipal` can set one,
and only its constructors can set its Bounds. `authz.FromContext` returns a
copy, and fails closed with `ErrUnauthenticated` when there's none.

**Refusals say little.** A caller only ever sees `unauthorized` or `forbidden`,
and the specific reason goes to the logs. Clerk's signing keys or API being
unreachable is a `503`, never a `401`, as it says nothing about the caller. A
limited token is refused with `403` before membership is looked at, unless the
request names one of its organizations, so a refusal says nothing about where
its user belongs. Its Principal carries the limit in `OrganizationLimit`.

**Tokens can't mint tokens.** Creating, listing, and revoking tokens refuse a
Principal with an `AccessTokenID`, so a leaked token can't mint more. Managing
tokens needs a session.

**End-to-end tests skip verification.** `AUTH_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFICATION`
accepts any session token unverified. The API refuses to start with it set
alongside any Clerk setting.

mechanisms.name: Authorization
mechanisms.description: Decides what a caller may do and which records they may do it to, from the Principal authentication built. It knows nothing of tokens or the database. What the terms mean in the domain is in the role and organization concepts.
mechanisms.body:
| Term | What it is | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Permission** | Something checked before doing it, as `resource:action`. Says what, never where | `authz.Catalog()` |
| **Platform role** | What people working with Exalynt may do when a request acts in no organization. A set of grants; a user holds at most one | `users.platform_role_id` |
| **Grant** | One permission at one scope, in a platform role | `authz.Grant` |
| **Scope** | How far a platform grant reaches from the caller: `global`, `team`, or `own`. Only platform roles have them | `authz/scope.go` |
| **Organization role** | What a member may do in that organization. A set of permissions; each membership holds one | `organization_members.role_id` |
| **Bounds** | The records a caller may act on with a permission: these organizations and users, or all | `authz.Bounds` |

A request's role turns into Bounds in the Principal: an organization role
bounds each permission to that organization, and a platform role resolves each
scope once, through its registry entry and `authz.Directory`. Services and
repositories only ever see Bounds, so a member's "this organization" and an
engineer's "my team's clients" are checked the same way.

A service requires the permission, then reads and writes within what it gets:

```go
bounds, err := authz.Require(ctx, authz.CapacitySchedule)  // ErrForbidden if not held
capacity, err := s.capacities.GetByID(ctx, bounds, id)     // ErrNotFound → ErrCapacityNotFound
```

Every table whose records a caller acts on directly has one bounds rule, beside
its columns: the condition matching a set of organizations, and the one
matching a set of users. `List` and `GetByID` both apply it. What hangs off a
